title: Addis Ababa Half-Day City Tour
teaser: Meet Lucy at the National Museum, stand beneath Holy Trinity’s stained glass and finish high on Entoto Hill above the capital.
overview: A half-day city tour of Addis Ababa offers a compact yet enriching glimpse into Ethiopia’s history, culture, and vibrant urban life. Begin your exploration at the National Museum of Ethiopia, a treasure trove of the country’s heritage, where you’ll encounter the famed fossilized remains of “Lucy” (Dinkinesh), a 3.2-million-year-old hominid, alongside ancient artifacts, royal regalia, and traditional art.

The museum’s four floors weave through Ethiopia’s prehistoric, medieval, and modern eras, providing context for its diverse cultural identity. From there, head to Holy Trinity Cathedral, an architectural gem and spiritual landmark adorned with stained glass, religious murals, and the tombs of Emperor Haile Selassie and other notable figures. Continue to Entoto Hill for panoramic views of the sprawling city and a glimpse into the 19th-century Entoto Maryam Church, once Emperor Menelik II’s palace.

Explore artifacts from prehistoric tools to royal treasures and modern history.

itinerary.title: National Museum of Ethiopia
paragraphs: A half-day city tour of Addis Ababa offers a captivating glimpse into Ethiopia’s rich history, culture, and natural beauty. Begin your journey at the National Museum of Ethiopia, where the legendary hominid fossil “Lucy” (Dinkinesh) takes center stage. This 3.2-million-year-old relic anchors a fascinating exploration of human evolution, complemented by four floors of artifacts spanning prehistoric tools, medieval royal treasures, vibrant traditional art, and exhibits tracing Ethiopia’s modern history. The museum serves as a gateway to understanding the nation’s layered identity, blending archaeology, ethnography, and artistry.

itinerary.title: Holy Trinity Cathedral
paragraphs: Next, immerse yourself in the spiritual and historical heart of the city at Holy Trinity Cathedral, an architectural marvel fusing Gothic arches with Ethiopian Orthodox motifs. Its vivid stained glass windows and intricate murals tell stories of faith and resilience, while the tombs of Emperor Haile Selassie, Empress Menen, and WWII heroes add a solemn yet inspiring historical dimension. Active worshippers and the scent of incense create an ambiance of reverence, making it a living testament to Ethiopia’s enduring religious traditions.

itinerary.title: Entoto Hill & Entoto Maryam
paragraphs: Conclude your tour with a visit to Entoto Hill, the city’s highest vantage point, offering sweeping panoramas of Addis Ababa’s sprawling landscape. Here, the 19th-century Entoto Maryam Church complex once Emperor Menelik II’s palace showcases traditional Ethiopian Orthodox architecture, with its circular design and vibrant religious artwork. Wander through fragrant eucalyptus forests and reflect on the hill’s legacy as the original capital before Addis Ababa’s founding, blending nature, history, and spirituality into a serene finale. This condensed itinerary packs centuries of heritage into a single morning or afternoon, leaving visitors with a profound appreciation for Ethiopia’s past and present.

title: Full-Day Addis Ababa Religious & Historical Tour
teaser: A day among the capital’s sacred places — St. George, Holy Trinity and the hilltop churches of Entoto — with a traditional lunch between.
overview: Addis Ababa, Ethiopia’s spiritual and historical heart, offers a captivating journey through its sacred landmarks and imperial legacy. This immersive tour begins at the majestic Holy Trinity Cathedral, a symbol of faith and resistance, where the tombs of Emperor Haile Selassie and stunning stained glass windows await. Explore the hidden Bata Mariam Church, with its unique rectangular design and royal connections to Emperor Menelik II, before visiting his final resting place at the Menelik Mausoleum. After a traditional Ethiopian lunch, delve into the iconic St. George Cathedral, celebrating Ethiopia’s victory at Adwa through its octagonal architecture and vibrant murals.

The adventure continues atop Entoto Mountain, where the serene Entoto Maryam Church and Menelik II’s rustic Old Palace offer panoramic views and a glimpse into Ethiopia’s imperial origins. From grand cathedrals to historic palaces, this tour unveils the city’s deep-rooted spirituality, royal heritage, and enduring national pride.

Bata Mariam Church – Menelik II’s personal place of worship
St. George Cathedral – Adwa victory memorial with vibrant art
Entoto Maryam Church – Mountain-top spiritual sanctuary
Menelik’s Palace – Birthplace of modern Addis Ababa

itinerary.title: Morning · Cathedrals of the capital
paragraphs: Begin your day with hotel pickup as we embark on a profound exploration of Addis Ababa’s most significant religious landmarks. Our first stop is the magnificent Holy Trinity Cathedral, the city’s most important Orthodox church, where you’ll admire its grand neo-Baroque architecture, exquisite stained glass windows, and the tombs of Emperor Haile Selassie and Empress Menen. Learn how this sacred site became a symbol of Ethiopian resistance and faith during the Italian occupation. Next, we visit the historic Bata Mariam Church within the Menelik Palace compound, a hidden gem where Emperor Menelik II worshipped. Marvel at its unique rectangular design (unlike traditional round churches), beautiful frescoes, and peaceful atmosphere. Nearby, explore the Menelik Mausoleum, final resting place of Ethiopia’s great emperor and other royals. After a traditional Ethiopian lunch (with vegetarian options available), we continue to the iconic St. George Cathedral, built to commemorate Ethiopia’s victory at Adwa. Its distinctive octagonal shape and vibrant murals tell stories of faith and national pride. See the museum’s collection of imperial crowns and religious artifacts.

itinerary.title: Afternoon · Entoto Mountain
paragraphs: In the afternoon, we ascend Entoto Mountain to visit the sacred Entoto Maryam Church, surrounded by fragrant eucalyptus forests. This spiritual retreat offers panoramic city views and houses fascinating historical relics. Nearby, step back in time at Emperor Menelik II’s Old Palace, a simple yet powerful reminder of Ethiopia’s imperial origins. This immersive experience reveals how faith shaped Ethiopia’s identity, from imperial times to today, with ample time at each location for reflection and photography. The tour concludes with evening drop-off at your hotel.

title: Half-Day Tour: National Museum & St. George Cathedral
teaser: Three million years in a morning: the fossils of the National Museum, then the cathedral built to celebrate the victory at Adwa.
overview: This enriching half-day tour begins with a convenient hotel pick-up, setting the stage for a fascinating journey through Ethiopia’s deep historical and spiritual heritage. You’ll start by visiting the iconic National Museum, which houses priceless artifacts that span thousands of years, including some of the most significant discoveries in human history.

Next, you’ll explore the striking St. George Cathedral, a revered symbol of faith and national pride. With expert guidance throughout the tour, you’ll uncover the powerful stories and cultural significance behind each site you visit.
The experience concludes with a comfortable return to your hotel, leaving you enriched and inspired by Ethiopia’s enduring cultural legacy.

itinerary.title: Hotel pick-up & the National Museum
paragraphs: Begin your enriching half-day journey with a convenient pick-up from your hotel, heading first to the National Museum of Ethiopia — the guardian of the nation’s most precious historical treasures. Here, you’ll come face-to-face with “Lucy” (Dinkinesh), the 3.2-million-year-old hominid whose discovery reshaped our understanding of human evolution.

itinerary.title: The paleontology galleries
paragraphs: The museum’s paleontological section takes you deep into Ethiopia’s ancient past with fossilized remains of early humans and prehistoric animals. The archaeological wing showcases Aksumite stelae, Sabaean inscriptions, and medieval artifacts that highlight Ethiopia’s glorious civilizations. You’ll also see royal regalia and ceremonial objects once belonging to Ethiopia’s emperors, including personal items of Emperor Haile Selassie, offering a direct connection to the country’s more recent imperial history. Throughout the visit, your expert guide will help you piece together how these exhibits reflect Ethiopia’s 3,000-year narrative as one of the world’s oldest continuous civilizations.

itinerary.title: St. George Cathedral
paragraphs: Next, continue to the iconic St. George Cathedral, a striking example of Ethiopian Orthodox architecture built in 1896 to commemorate the country’s historic victory at the Battle of Adwa. The cathedral’s distinctive octagonal design, painted in the vibrant colors of the Ethiopian flag — green, yellow, and red — immediately captures your attention. Inside, light pours through stained-glass windows, illuminating murals that depict vivid biblical scenes and honored Ethiopian saints.

itinerary.title: The cathedral museum
paragraphs: The cathedral houses priceless religious artifacts, including ceremonial crosses and hand-written bibles. Its museum features treasures such as Emperor Menelik II’s coronation robes and other royal relics. As you tread the same stone paths where Emperor Haile Selassie was crowned, your guide will share inspiring stories about how this sacred site has become a powerful symbol of Ethiopian faith, resistance, and national identity.

itinerary.title: Return to your hotel
paragraphs: The tour concludes with a comfortable drop-off at your hotel, leaving you with deep cultural insights and a profound appreciation for Ethiopia’s extraordinary fusion of ancient history and living spiritual traditions.

title: Half-Day Tour: The Jubilee Palace
teaser: Inside Emperor Haile Selassie’s restored 1955 palace — the Green Salon, the mirrored banquet hall and the imperial throne.
overview: Addis Ababa whose name means ‘New Flower’. Founded in 1887 by Emperor Menelik II, it is today a political and business capital home to the headquarters of the African Union and to one of the largest number of diplomatic missions in the world. Situated in the highlands – at 2300m – with a year round balmy climate.

Addis is a cosmopolitan mix of East and West where you will find interesting historic churches and mosques, museums, monuments and landmarks, and public parks alongside stylish new cafes, international hotels and restaurants. Not to be missed are the cultural restaurants serving the unique Ethiopian cuisine accompanied by traditional music and dance.

itinerary.title: Arrival at the Jubilee Palace
paragraphs: Discover the grandeur of Ethiopia’s modern imperial legacy with a captivating half-day tour of the newly opened Jubilee Palace—an architectural masterpiece that once served as the official residence of Emperor Haile Selassie. Your journey begins with a convenient hotel pick-up, leading to a guided exploration of this meticulously restored landmark, which now functions as the Prime Minister’s office while offering limited public access to its historic interiors.

itinerary.title: The state rooms
paragraphs: Marvel at the palace’s striking neo-Baroque façade, a harmonious blend of Ethiopian symbolism and European design, commissioned to celebrate the Emperor’s Silver Jubilee in 1955. Inside, you’ll step into regal spaces such as the magnificent Green Salon with its exquisite stained-glass dome, the elegant Mirrored Banquet Hall that once hosted royal receptions, and the Emperor’s private chapel, preserved in its original sanctity.

itinerary.title: Stories, artefacts & the palace gardens
paragraphs: As you explore, your expert guide will share compelling stories about the palace’s significance during the Derg regime, its careful restoration process, and the priceless artifacts housed within—including the original imperial throne, diplomatic gifts from world leaders, and grand murals narrating Ethiopia’s rich history. The tour concludes with a serene stroll through the manicured palace gardens, offering beautiful photo opportunities amidst fountains and vibrant floral displays, before your comfortable return to the hotel.

title: Day Trip to Adadi Mariam & Tiya Stelae
teaser: A rock-hewn church in the Lalibela tradition and a UNESCO field of carved stelae, an easy day south of Addis Ababa.
overview: South of Addis Ababa, two remarkable places sit within an hour of each other. Adadi Mariam is a 12th-century church carved down into the rock, traditionally attributed to King Lalibela himself, and still in daily use by the local community.
A little further on, the UNESCO-listed field at Tiya holds dozens of ancient standing stones engraved with swords and enigmatic symbols — among the most mysterious monuments in the Horn of Africa.

Tiya Stelae Field a UNESCO World Heritage Site featuring 36 ancient stone pillars.
Local Cuisine Enjoy a picnic lunch or taste traditional Ethiopian dishes like injera and stews.
Great Rift Valley Views tunning panoramas on the return journey.

itinerary.title: Adadi Mariam rock-hewn church
paragraphs: Start on a day trip from Addis Ababa to explore the historical wonders of Adadi Mariam Church and Tiya Stelae Field. The journey begins with an early morning pickup from your hotel or the airport in a private, air-conditioned vehicle. Located approximately 60 km southwest of Addis Ababa, Adadi Mariam Church is a 13th-century rock-hewn church carved by King Lalibela. It showcases intricate stone architecture and remains an active place of worship. Visitors are required to remove their shoes before entering, and women are advised to cover their heads as a sign of respect while exploring the church and its serene surroundings.

itinerary.title: Tiya Stelae Field (UNESCO)
paragraphs: Continuing south for about 35 km, you will arrive at the UNESCO-listed Tiya Stelae Field, home to 36 ancient stone pillars adorned with enigmatic carvings of swords and symbols. These monuments are believed to mark a 12th–14th-century burial site, offering fascinating insights into Ethiopia’s pre-Christian past. Along the way, you can enjoy a picnic lunch or stop at a local restaurant to savor traditional Ethiopian dishes like injera, a fermented flatbread, served with flavorful stews.

itinerary.title: Rift Valley views & the drive home
paragraphs: On the return journey, take in the breathtaking panoramic views of the Great Rift Valley. If time permits, visit a nearby village to experience daily Ethiopian life or participate in a traditional coffee ceremony, a cherished cultural ritual. The trip concludes back in Addis Ababa, where you will be dropped off at your hotel.

title: Day Trip to Wenchi Crater Lake
teaser: Descend into an extinct volcano, row out to an island monastery and ride back up the crater wall on horseback.
overview: Wenchi Crater Lake is a stunning volcanic lake surrounded by lush forests, waterfalls, and hot springs. The lake’s crystal-clear turquoise waters reflect the surrounding green hills, creating a postcard-perfect scene. Visitors can hike or ride horses down the crater’s 4-kilometer trail, passing traditional Oromo villages, terraced farmlands, and volcanic landscapes . The lake itself is one of Africa’s cleanest, with mineral-rich waters that change color from blue in the morning to green in the afternoon.

Wenchi was named UNWTO’s Best Tourist Village in 2021 for its pristine environment, welcoming locals, and sustainable tourism efforts. The community actively preserves the lake’s cleanliness, banning litter and Motorized boats.
highlights: Boat rides to Cherkos Monastery on Debre Island.
Horseback riding through villages and crater trails.
Hiking to waterfalls, hot springs, and volcanic viewpoints.
Cultural interactions with Oromo and Amhara communities.
Photography of the beautiful Landscape and lake.

itinerary.title: Through Menagesha to the crater rim
paragraphs: Start your day early with a drive from Addis Ababa through green mountains and forests. You will pass beautiful places like Menagesha Forest, the old town of Addis Alem, and Ambo (famous for its natural spring water). When you arrive at Wenchi Crater Lake, local guides will explain the trip. You can choose to hike down into the crater or ride a horse (or drive down if you prefer). The path takes you through small villages, farms, and volcanic land. You’ll see special plants and meet friendly people living there.

itinerary.title: Boat to Debre Cherkos Monastery
paragraphs: At the bottom of the crater, enjoy a peaceful boat ride on the lake’s blue-green water to visit Debre Island. Here, you can explore the Cherkos Monastery, a quiet religious place built in the 13th century. Afterward, have a picnic lunch by the lake. Relax, swim in warm natural hot springs, Walk around the crater floor, or just enjoy the calm views.

itinerary.title: Hike or ride out of the crater
paragraphs: To leave the crater, you can hike back up, ride a horse, or take a mule. On the way, stop to take photos of the amazing views—green valleys, the volcano crater, and the lake below.

itinerary.title: Back to Addis Ababa
paragraphs: Finally, drive back to Addis Ababa through small villages and countryside. Think about your day: the kind locals, the beautiful nature, and how the community works with tourists to protect the area (they offer horse rides, guided tours, and sell honey in certain seasons).

title: Day Trip to Debre Libanos & the Blue Nile Gorge
teaser: Across the Sululta plains to a 13th-century monastery, gelada baboons on the cliff edge and the old Portuguese Bridge.
overview: The tour to Debre Libanos Monastery and the Jemma River Gorge offers a captivating blend of Ethiopian religious history, stunning natural landscapes, and cultural immersion, all within a day trip from Addis Ababa. You’ll journey through picturesque highlands to reach the significant Debre Libanos Monastery, steeped in centuries of tradition and adorned with beautiful architecture and religious art. The adventure continues to the dramatic Jemma River Gorge, where you can marvel at the vast escarpment, the historic Portuguese Bridge, and the unique wildlife, including Gelada baboons. Opportunities to engage with local culture, such as a traditional coffee ceremony, may also be part of the experience, providing a well-rounded glimpse into Ethiopia’s rich heritage and natural beauty.
highlights: Visit Debre Libanos Monastery: Explore this significant Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo monastery founded by Saint Tekle Haymanot in the 13th century, observing its religious importance and architectural beauty.
Discover the new church: See the modern church within the monastery grounds, often adorned with intricate artwork and reflecting Ethiopian religious art and history.
Explore Saint Tekle Haymanot’s Cave (optional): Some tours include a visit to the cave where the saint is believed to have meditated for many years.
See the Monastery Museum: View religious artifacts, historical manuscripts, and other relics preserved within the monastery’s museum.
Witness the Jemma River Gorge: Marvel at the breathtaking panoramic views of the deep and expansive Jemma River Gorge.
Visit the Portuguese Bridge: Observe the 16th-century bridge (likely Ethiopian-built) spanning a tributary, offering a historical perspective and scenic viewpoints.
Wildlife Spotting: Keep an eye out for indigenous wildlife, particularly the Gelada baboons, which are commonly found in the gorge area.
Scenic Drive through Sululta Plains: Enjoy the picturesque landscapes and potential birdwatching opportunities during the drive to and from the sites.

itinerary.title: Sululta plains & Debre Libanos Monastery
paragraphs: A journey to Debre Libanos Monastery and the Jemma River Gorge typically involves a drive north from Addis Ababa, passing through the Sululta plains with opportunities for birdwatching. The first major stop is the Debre Libanos Monastery, a significant religious center in Ethiopian Orthodox Christianity founded in the 13th century by Saint Tekle Haymanot. Visitors can explore the monastery grounds, the new church built by Emperor Haile Selassie, and perhaps visit the cave where the saint is said to have prayed. The monastery also houses a museum with religious artifacts and historical relics.

itinerary.title: Jemma Gorge & the Portuguese Bridge
paragraphs: Continuing the journey, the breathtaking Jemma River Gorge unfolds, offering dramatic escarpment views. A notable point of interest is the 16th-century Portuguese Bridge (though its construction was likely by Ethiopians), which spans a tributary of the Blue Nile and provides stunning vantage points of the deep gorge. The area is also known for its diverse birdlife and the chance to spot Gelada baboons, a primate species endemic to the Ethiopian Highlands. Some itineraries include a visit to a local Oromo family and participation in a traditional Ethiopian coffee ceremony, offering a glimpse into the local culture. The Jemma River itself is a significant tributary of the Blue Nile, carving a deep and impressive valley through the landscape.

title: 2 Days Awash National Park
teaser: Oryx on the Ilala Sala plains, the falls of the Awash River and a warm soak at the Doho hot springs.
overview: This 2 day trip takes you from Addis Ababa to Awash National Park, one of Ethiopia’s best wildlife destinations. You will travel through scenic landscapes, spotting volcanic formations, valleys, and small villages along the way. In Awash National Park, you will explore diverse wildlife, including gazelles, baboons, and oryx, and visit the stunning Awash Falls, a beautiful waterfall in the park.

On the second day, a morning safari will give you a chance to see more animals in their natural habitat before heading back to Addis Ababa. Along the return journey, you can stop in Bishoftu, a town famous for its beautiful lakes, where you can relax and enjoy a lakeside meal. Your trip will end with wonderful memories of nature, wildlife, and Ethiopia’s breathtaking landscapes.

itinerary.title: Addis Ababa – Awash National Park
paragraphs: You will start your journey from Addis Ababa and travel to Awash National Park. The drive will take you through beautiful landscapes, including volcanic mountains and valleys. Along the way, you can stop for lunch and enjoy the view. Once you arrive at Awash, you will explore the park, which is home to many animals like baboons, gazelles, and oryx. You will also see the famous Awash Falls, a stunning waterfall inside the park. In the evening, you can relax at your accommodation and enjoy the peaceful surroundings.

itinerary.title: Awash National Park – Addis Ababa
paragraphs: You will wake up early for a morning safari in Awash National Park. This is the best time to see wildlife, as many animals are active in the morning. After the safari, you will start your journey back to Addis Ababa. On the way, you can stop at Bishoftu, a town known for its beautiful lakes. Here, you can have lunch by the lakeside and enjoy the view. After lunch, you will continue your drive and arrive in Addis Ababa in the late afternoon, ending your trip with wonderful memories.
itinerary.overnight: End of tour, hotel or Departure.

excluded: Any service not mentioned in the “Price included” section

title: 3 Days Historic Harar & Dire Dawa
teaser: The walled Muslim city of Harar, its hyena men and spice markets, with colonial-era Dire Dawa on the way.
overview: This 3-day trip takes you from Ethiopia’s modern capital, Addis Ababa, to the magical ancient city of Harar. You’ll experience Ethiopia’s rich culture, history, and unique traditions. Highlights include exploring Harar’s UNESCO-listed old town with its colorful houses and narrow streets, watching local people feed wild hyenas at night, and shopping for handmade crafts and coffee in lively markets. The trip includes short flights, scenic drives, and unforgettable moments in one of Africa’s most historic and fascinating cities. Perfect for: Travelers who love history, culture, and adventure!
highlights: Harar’s ancient walled city** (UNESCO site).
Explore colorful alleyways, mosques, and traditional Harari houses.
Hyena Men experience – watch locals feed wild hyenas at dusk!
Shop for handmade crafts, baskets, and Ethiopian coffee in Harar’s markets.
Learn Harari culture at the Harari Cultural Museum.
Scenic drives and glimpses of Dire Dawa’s historic architecture.

itinerary.title: Addis Ababa – Dire Dawa (flight) – Harar
paragraphs: You will start your journey with a short morning flight from Addis Ababa (Ethiopia’s capital) to Dire Dawa, a lively city with busy markets. From Dire Dawa, you will drive to Harar, a very old city with historic walls. Harar is famous for its colorful houses, narrow streets, and many mosques. Spend your first day exploring the city’s unique atmosphere.

itinerary.title: Harar
paragraphs: Today, you will discover more of Harar, a UNESCO world heritage site. Visit the Harari Cultural Museum to learn about local traditions, shop for handmade crafts and fresh coffee in the markets, and watch an exciting evening ritual where local people feed wild hyenas outside the city walls. This is a special experience you will never forget!

itinerary.title: Harar – Dire Dawa – Addis Ababa (flight)
paragraphs: On your final day, return to Dire Dawa by road. If there is time, you can see the city’s old train station or historic buildings before flying back to Addis Ababa. You will leave with amazing memories of Harar’s culture, history, and natural beauty.

excluded: Any service not mentioned in the “Price included” section

title: 3 Days Lalibela
teaser: A short, focused journey to the eleven rock-hewn churches of Lalibela, with time for the mountain monastery of Asheten Mariam.
overview: Lalibela, Ethiopia’s most treasured historical site, often called Africa’s Petra* Over three days, you will explore the incredible rock-hewn churches, marvel at their centuries-old craftsmanship, and witness the deeply spiritual traditions of Ethiopian Orthodox Christianity. From the famous Bete Giorgis to the hidden gems outside the town, Lalibela’s stunning architecture and serene landscapes offer a truly unforgettable experience. The tour concludes with a return flight to Addis Ababa, where you can enjoy some last-minute sightseeing or shopping before departure.
highlights: Rock-hewn churches, 11 unique monolithic churches, a UNESCO World Heritage site.
Bete Giorgis The most iconic cross-shaped church, carved into rock.
Yemrehanna Kristos a cave church with intricate architectural details.
Local spirituality witness centuries-old Ethiopian Orthodox practices.

itinerary.title: Addis Ababa – Lalibela (flight)
paragraphs: After breakfast, take a short flight to Lalibela. After checking in at the hotel, visit the rock-hewn Churches of Lalibela. Lalibela is the jewel in the crown of Ethiopia, home to the most famous churches and the scene of many major religious ceremonies. Also known as ‘Africa’s Petra’, Lalibela and its rock-hewn churches are among Ethiopia’s top attractions. Visit the churches: Bete Medhane Alem, Bete Mariam, Bete Maskal, Bete Danaghel, Bete Golgotha & Bete Mikael, and Bete Giorgis. In the afternoon, visit the remaining churches: Bete Amanuel, Bete Markorios, Bete Aba Libanos, and Bete Gebriel-Rufael.

itinerary.title: Lalibela
paragraphs: After breakfast, visit the rest of the rock-hewn churches of Lalibela and take an excursion to visit some of the churches outside Lalibela town.

itinerary.title: Lalibela – Addis Ababa (flight)
paragraphs: Take a morning flight back to Addis Ababa, where you can enjoy some last-minute shopping or sightseeing before your departure.

excluded: Any expenses which is not stated above

title: 5 Days Historic North
teaser: Bahir Dar, Gondar and Lalibela by air — the great sights of the Historic Route in under a week.
overview: The essentials of Ethiopia’s Historic Route in five days. Fly to Bahir Dar for the island monasteries of Lake Tana and the Blue Nile Falls, continue to the royal castles of Gondar, then end among the rock-hewn churches of Lalibela.
Domestic flights keep the pace comfortable, leaving the time for the places themselves.
highlights: Explore the vibrant city of Bahir Dar, nestled on the shores of Lake Tana.
Embark on a boat trip to visit the fascinating monasteries on the lake’s islands.
Witness the breathtaking Blue Nile Falls.
“Camelot of Africa,” Gondar, with its well-preserved 17th-century castles and palaces.
The Royal Enclosure, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Explore the fascinating Debre Berhan Selassie Church.
Rock-hewn churches of Lalibela, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

itinerary.title: Addis Ababa
paragraphs: After checking in at the hotel and having breakfast, embark on a sightseeing tour of Addis Ababa. Drive north to Mount Entoto to visit a museum, a church, and Emperor Menelik’s Palace. Then descend to the city and proceed to the Ethnographic Museum, which showcases a large collection of Ethiopian crafts and items of historical interest.

Continue the tour to the Holy Trinity Cathedral, the highest-ranking Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo cathedral in Addis Ababa. Built in 1941 to commemorate Ethiopia’s victory over Italian occupation, this cathedral remains an important place of worship.
After lunch, visit the National Museum, home to the famous 3.2 million-year-old hominid fossil, Lucy, along with other significant archaeological findings.

itinerary.title: Addis Ababa – Bahir Dar (flight)
paragraphs: In the morning, take a flight to Bahir Dar. After checking in at the hotel, enjoy a private boat ride on Lake Tana to visit Ura Kidane Mehret Church, located on the Zege Peninsula. Founded in the 14th century, the present circular church dates back to the 16th century and is adorned with murals painted between 100 and 250 years ago.
After lunch, drive to the village of Tis Isat to witness the breathtaking Blue Nile Falls. After the visit, return to Bahir Dar.

itinerary.title: Bahir Dar – Gondar
paragraphs: After breakfast, drive to Gondar, the 17th-century capital of Ethiopia. In the afternoon, visit the Imperial Castle Compound, the Bath of Emperor Fasiladas, Quskuam Mariam Church (the residence of Empress Mintwab), and the renowned Debre Birhan Selassie Church, famous for its stunning wall and ceiling paintings.

itinerary.title: Gondar – Lalibela (flight)
paragraphs: After breakfast, take a flight to Lalibela via Woreta, passing through the picturesque Amhara region. Enjoy stunning views of the Guna Mountains as you travel through this dramatic highland landscape.

itinerary.title: Lalibela – Addis Ababa (flight)
paragraphs: After breakfast, fly back to Addis Ababa. In the evening, enjoy a farewell dinner at one of the best traditional restaurants in the city, accompanied by cultural music, dance performances, and delicious Ethiopian cuisine.
itinerary.overnight: Overnight in Addis Ababa or Departure.

title: 7 Days Historic North with the Simien Mountains
teaser: Castles, monasteries and rock churches — plus a day on the Simien escarpment among gelada baboons.
overview: A week that pairs Ethiopia’s great history with one of Africa’s great landscapes. Alongside Lake Tana, Gondar and Lalibela, you’ll spend a day in the Simien Mountains National Park, walking the edge of the escarpment among herds of endemic gelada baboons.
It is the ideal first trip to Ethiopia for travellers who want both culture and nature.
highlights: Explore the vibrant city of Bahir Dar, nestled on the shores of Lake Tana.
Embark on a boat trip to visit the fascinating monasteries on the lake’s islands.
Witness the breathtaking Blue Nile Falls.
“Camelot of Africa,” Gondar, with its well-preserved 17th-century castles and palaces.
The Royal Enclosure, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Explore the fascinating Debre Berhan Selassie Church.
Rock-hewn churches of Lalibela, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

itinerary.title: Addis Ababa
paragraphs: After checking in at the hotel and having breakfast, embark on a sightseeing tour of Addis. Drive up north to Mount Entoto to visit a museum, a church, and Emperor Menelik Palace. Descend to Addis and proceed to the Ethnographic Museum, which displays a large collection of Ethiopian crafts and items of historical interest. Continue to visit the Trinity Cathedral, the highest-ranking Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo cathedral in Addis Ababa, built in 1941 to commemorate the Ethiopian victory over Italian occupation. It is an important place of worship in Ethiopia. After lunch, visit the National Museum that houses the 3.2 million-year-old fossils of ‘Lucy’, possibly our earliest ancestor, along with other fascinating archaeological findings.

itinerary.title: Addis Ababa – Bahir Dar (flight)
paragraphs: In the morning, take the flight to Bahir Dar. After checking in at the hotel, take a private boat to Ura Kidane Mehret Ethiopian Orthodox Church, located on the Zege Peninsula around Lake Tana. Founded in the 14th century, the present circular church dates from the 16th century, with its interior decorated with numerous murals painted between 100 and 250 years ago. After lunch, drive to the village of Tis Isat to see the Blue Nile Falls. After the visit, return to Bahir Dar.

itinerary.title: Bahir Dar – Gondar
paragraphs: After breakfast, drive to Gondar, the 17th-century capital of Ethiopia. In the afternoon, visit the Imperial Castle Compound, the Bath of Emperor Fasiladas, the Church of Quskuam Mariam, the residence of Empress Mintwab, and the Church of Debre Birhan Sillassie, famous for its wall and ceiling paintings.

itinerary.title: Gondar – Simien Mountains – Gondar
paragraphs: After breakfast, drive from Gondar to Debark, the headquarters of the Simien Mountains National Park. Stop here to get permission to enter the park and meet the scout. From Debark, drive to the park gate, about 16km away, and then head 6km to Buit Ras, the first area of the national park. Trek for about 3-4 hours to Chilkuwanit, one of the most beautiful viewpoints, offering stunning views over the escarpment. You will encounter troops of endemic Gelada Baboons and may see jackals, klipspringers, and various birds. Afterward, return to Gondar.

itinerary.title: Gondar – Lalibela (drive)
paragraphs: After breakfast, drive to Lalibela via Woreta, passing through the Amhara state. Enjoy stunning views of the Guna Mountains as you travel through this dramatic landscape.

itinerary.title: Lalibela
paragraphs: After breakfast, visit the rock-hewn Churches of Lalibela, often called ‘Africa’s Petra’. Lalibela and its churches are among Ethiopia’s top attractions. Visit the rock-hewn Churches including Bete Medhane Alem, Bete Mariam, Bete Maskal, Bete Danaghel, Bete Golgotha & Bete Mikael, and Bete Giorgis. In the afternoon, visit the remaining churches: Bete Amanuel, Bete Markorios, Bete Aba Libanos, and Bete Gebriel-Rufael.

itinerary.title: Lalibela – Addis Ababa (flight)
paragraphs: After breakfast, take the flight back to Addis Ababa. In the evening, enjoy a farewell dinner at one of the best traditional restaurants in Addis Ababa, with cultural music, dance, and traditional Ethiopian foods.
itinerary.overnight: Overnight Addis Ababa, Hotel or Departure.

title: 7 Days Rock-Hewn Churches of Tigray
teaser: Cliff-top churches of Gheralta, the stelae of Axum and the ancient mosque of Negash — the far north at its most dramatic.
overview: This tour takes you on an exciting journey through Ethiopia’s most famous historical and cultural sites. You will start in Addis Ababa, visiting the National Museum to see “Lucy,” the oldest human skeleton, and explore beautiful churches and busy markets.

Then, fly to Tigray to see amazing rock churches carved into mountains, some with colorful paintings over 1,000 years old. You will climb (with help from local guides) to reach some of these hidden treasures, enjoying incredible views along the way.
Next, travel to Axum, an ancient city full of mystery, where you will see giant stone obelisks, the ruins of the Queen of Sheba’s palace, and a sacred church said to protect the Ark of the Covenant.

Finally, return to Addis Ababa for a farewell dinner with traditional food, music, and dancing. This tour is a perfect mix of adventure, history, and culture great for travelers who want to see Ethiopia’s most unforgettable places!
highlights: See “Lucy,” the 3.2-million-year-old skeleton, at the National Museum.
Visit the beautiful Holy Trinity Cathedral (Emperor Haile Selassie’s burial place).
Enjoy panoramic city views from Mount Entoto.
Discover ancient churches carved into mountains, like Michael Imba, Abraha We Atsbeha, and Wikro Kirkos.
Climb (with local guides) to Abune Yemata Guh, a cliffside church with 5th-century frescoes.
Visit Mariam Korkor, another stunning church with breathtaking views.
See the Giant Obelisks, royal tombs over 1,700 years old.
Explore the ruins of the Queen of Sheba’s Palace.
Visit Tsion Mariam Church, believed to house the Ark of the Covenant.
Stop at Yeha Temple, Ethiopia’s oldest standing structure (500 BC).
Climb (men only) to Debre Damo Monastery using a leather rope.

itinerary.title: Addis Ababa
paragraphs: Welcome to Addis Ababa! Your day begins with a fascinating tour of Ethiopia’s vibrant capital. We’ll start at the National Museum, where you’ll meet “Lucy,” the famous 3.2-million-year-old skeleton that tells us so much about human origins. Next, we visit the beautiful Holy Trinity Cathedral, an important religious site with stunning stained glass windows and the final resting place of Emperor Haile Selassie. Then we’ll drive up to Mount Entoto, where you can enjoy fresh mountain air and breathtaking views over the entire city. Finally, we’ll experience the lively chaos of Merkato Market, Africa’s largest open-air market, where you can shop for traditional Ethiopian coffee, colorful fabrics, and handmade crafts while soaking up the local atmosphere.

itinerary.title: Addis Ababa – Fly to Mekelle – drive to Wukro
paragraphs: After breakfast, we’ll take a short flight north to Mekelle, the gateway to Tigray’s ancient rock churches. From here, our journey continues by road to Wikro, where we’ll step back in time at three incredible rock-hewn churches. First is Michael Imba, carved entirely into a mountainside with well-preserved frescoes. Next comes Abraha We Atsbeha, one of Tigray’s largest and most impressive churches, named after a legendary Axumite king. We finish at Wukro Kirkos, a smaller but beautifully decorated church tucked into the cliffs. Each site offers a unique glimpse into Ethiopia’s deep Christian heritage and amazing architectural skills from centuries ago.

itinerary.title: Wukro
paragraphs: Today we continue discovering Tigray’s spectacular rock churches, starting with Medhanialem Adikesho. Reaching this church involves a short but rewarding hike, with panoramic views as your reward. Inside, you’ll find ancient biblical paintings still vibrant after centuries. After lunch, we visit Abune Abraham, dramatically perched on a cliff edge. The climb up is adventurous (with local guides assisting), but the church’s interior, filled with precious religious art, makes it unforgettable. These hidden gems show how early Christians created sacred spaces in these remote mountains.

itinerary.title: Wukro – Hawzen
paragraphs: After breakfast drive to Hawzenn prepare for today’s highlight: two of Ethiopia’s most breathtaking churches. First is Abune Yemata Guh, where a thrilling (but safe) 20-minute climb up a rock face leads to a church literally carved into a sheer cliff. It takes 1 hour to climb the cliffs totally. The effort is rewarded with 360-degree mountain views and stunning 5th-century frescoes. After descending, we visit Mariam Korkor, another cliffside masterpiece with a large interior and more ancient artwork. Local priests will share stories about these sacred places that have hosted prayers for over 1,500 years.

itinerary.title: Hawzen – Axum
paragraphs: On this day leaving the cliffs behind, we journey toward Axum, Ethiopia’s most ancient city. Our first stop is Debre Damo, a monastery accessible only by climbing a 15-meter leather rope (men only; women can explore the base). This 6th-century site preserves unique architecture and manuscripts. Next is Yeha Temple, Ethiopia’s oldest standing structure dating back to 500 BC. This massive stone ruin from the pre-Christian Sabaean civilization shows intricate masonry work that still puzzles historians today.

itinerary.title: Axum
paragraphs: Today we immerse ourselves in Axum’s legendary history. We begin at Tsion Mariam Church, believed to house the Biblical Ark of the Covenant in its heavily guarded chapel. Nearby stand the giant Axum Obelisks – towering 1,700-year-old stone monuments marking royal tombs. At the Queen of Sheba’s Palace ruins, you’ll walk through the remains of what was once a magnificent palace, linked to Ethiopia’s most famous ancient ruler. The Axum Museum ties everything together with artifacts from these sites, including ancient coins and royal inscriptions. We don’t miss King Ezana’s Stone, a 4th-century tablet written in three ancient languages.

itinerary.title: Axum – Addis Ababa (flight)
paragraphs: After breakfast, we catch our flight back to Addis Ababa. If time permits, you might do some last-minute shopping at souvenir shops or visit a traditional coffee house for one final cup of Ethiopia’s famous coffee before your onward journey. In the evening before your departure, enjoy a farewell dinner at one of the best traditional restaurants in Addis Ababa, with cultural music, dance, and traditional Ethiopian foods.

excluded: Any service not mentioned in the “Price included” section

title: 9 Days Historic North
teaser: The full Historic Route — Bahir Dar, Gondar, the Simien Mountains, Axum and Lalibela — at an unhurried pace.
overview: The historical northern circuit of Ethiopia offers a captivating journey through time, showcasing ancient civilizations, stunning landscapes, and unique cultural experiences. Gondar, with its castles and palaces; Lalibela, with its remarkable rock-hewn churches; Negash, one of the earliest holy Muslim centres from the Prophet Muhammad Era with the Negash Amedin Mesgid. Lake Tana, source of the Blue Nile, is the largest lake with 37 islands and the Monasteries like Kibran Gebriel and Kidanemhiret dating back to 14th century.
highlights: Explore the vibrant city of Bahir Dar, nestled on the shores of Lake Tana.
Embark on a boat trip to visit the fascinating monasteries on the lake’s islands.
Witness the breathtaking Blue Nile Falls.
“Camelot of Africa,” Gondar, with its well-preserved 17th-century castles and palaces.
The Royal Enclosure, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Explore the fascinating Debre Berhan Selassie Church.
Breathtaking trek through the Simien Mountains.
Axum, the ancient capital of the Kingdom of Aksum.
Rock-hewn churches of Lalibela, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

itinerary.title: Addis Ababa
paragraphs: After checking the hotel and breakfast, on a sightseeing of Addis, drive up north to Mount Entoto to visit a museum, church and Emperor Menelik Palace. Descending down to Addis, proceed to the Ethnographic museum, which displays a very large collection of Ethiopian crafts and items of historical interest. Continue to visit the Trinity Cathedral, the highest ranking Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo cathedral in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. This was built in 1941 to commemorate the Ethiopian victory over Italian occupation and is an important place of worship in Ethiopia. After lunch, proceed to the National museum that houses the 3.2 million years old fossils of ‘Lucy’ (perhaps our earliest ancestor) is among other interesting archeological findings.

itinerary.title: Addis Ababa – Bahir Dar (flight)
paragraphs: In the morning we take the morning flight to Bahir Dar. After check in the hotel we take private boat to Ura Kidane Mehret Ethiopian Orthodox Church, located on the Zege peninsula around Lake Tana in Ethiopia. The most attractive church in the Lake Tana region founded in the 14th century although the present circular church dates from the 16th century. Its interior is decorated with numerous murals painted between 100 and 250 years ago. In the afternoon after lunch we drive to the village of Tis Isat to see the Blue Nile falls. After visit drive back to Bahir dar.

itinerary.title: Bahir Dar – Gondar
paragraphs: After breakfast drive from to Gondar – the 17th century capital of Ethiopia. In the afternoon, visit the Imperial Castle Compound of Gondar, the ‘Bath of Emperor Fasiladas’, the church of QuskuamMariam, the residence of Empress Mintwab, and the church of DebreBirhan Sillassie which is famous for its wall and ceiling paintings.

itinerary.title: Gondar – Simien Mountains National Park
paragraphs: After breakfast drive from Gondar to Debark, which is the headquarter town for the national park. We will stop here to get a permission to enter the park and meet the scout. From Debark town, we will drive to the park gate, which is about 16km from the town. Then, we are heading about 6km to Buit Ras, the first area of the national park. From Buit Ras, we will trek for about 3, 4 hours to Chilkuwanit which is one of the most beautiful viewpoints. This area offers stunning views over the escarpment dropping vertically. You will most certainly encounter troops of the endemic Gelada Baboons and see them up-close. You may also see common jackal, klipspringer and more. There are a lot of birds such as Thick-billed Raven, Augar Buzard, Black Kites, Lammergeyer and different plant species such as Abyssinian Rose, Erica Arboria tree, Euphorbia Species, St. Johns Worttree (Hypercumrevoltum) and so on.

itinerary.title: Simien Mountains National Park – Axum
paragraphs: In the morning, drive to Axum, enjoying spectacular views of the Simien Mountains. After stopping for lunch in Adarky, proceed driving through the Tekeze Valley to Axum, home of the ancient Axumite Empire, the Queen of Sheba, and the Ark of the Covenant.

itinerary.title: Axum
paragraphs: Morning after breakfast explores the city of Axum. Axum, the ancient capital of the Kingdom of Aksum. Visit the Stelae Park, home to massive obelisks, some of the largest stone monuments ever erected. Explore the King Kaleb and Gebre Meskel Tomb, a royal burial site. In the afternoon, visit St. Mary of Zion Church, believed to house the Ark of the Covenant.

itinerary.title: Axum – Lalibela (flight)
paragraphs: On this day after breakfast take a short flight to Lalibela. After check in the hotel start to visit the rock-hewn Churches of Lalibela. Lalibela is the jewel in the crown of Ethiopia, the home of the most famous churches and the scene of so many major religious ceremonies. Also known as ‘Africa’s Petra’, Lalibela and its rock-hewn Churches are arguably Ethiopia’s top most attractions. Visit the rock-hewn Churches. These Churches include Bete Medhane Alem, Bete Mariam, Bete Maskal, Bete Danaghel, Bete Golgotha & Bete Mikael, and Bete Giorgis. Afternoon, you will visit the rest of the rock hewn churches of Lalibela i.e. Bete Amanuel, Bete Markorios, Bete Aba Libanos, and Bete Gebriel-Rufael.

itinerary.title: Lalibela
paragraphs: On this day after breakfast we start to visit the rest of the rock-hewn Churches of Lalibela and an excursion to visit some of the churches outside Lalibela town.

itinerary.title: Lalibela – Addis Ababa (flight)
paragraphs: Fly back to Addis Ababa. In the afternoon, visit the Merkato, the largest open-air market in Africa. Enjoy a farewell dinner with traditional Ethiopian cuisine and cultural performances.
itinerary.overnight: Overnight, Addis Ababa hotel or Departure.

title: 13 Days Historic North
teaser: Every great site of northern Ethiopia, from Lake Tana to the cliff churches of Tigray, with time to linger in each.
overview: This unforgettable 13-day journey through Ethiopia, a land where ancient history and stunning natural beauty converge. This immersive tour takes you from the bustling capital of Addis Ababa, home to the ancient “Lucy,” to the tranquil island monasteries of Lake Tana and the thundering Blue Nile Falls. Explore the majestic castles of Gondar, venture into the dramatic Simien Mountains National Park to encounter unique wildlife like the Gelada Baboons, and delve into the profound historical and religious heritage of Axum, with its colossal stelae. Experience the exhilarating rock-hewn churches of Tigray’s Gheralta Mountains before culminating your adventure in Lalibela, the “Eighth Wonder of the World,” where awe-inspiring churches are carved directly from living rock, leaving an indelible impression of Ethiopia’s rich past and vibrant present.
highlights: “Lucy,” visit Holy Trinity Cathedral, explore Merkato (Africa’s largest market).
Boat trip on Lake Tana to ancient island churches, witness Blue Nile Falls.
Explore 17th-century castles and famous painted churches.
Trek stunning landscapes, spot unique Gelada Baboons.
Marvel at ancient stelae, visit Queen Sheba’s Palace and historic churches.
Discover amazing rock-hewn churches, some requiring exciting climbs.
Explore the “8th Wonder of the World” incredible rock-hewn churches.

itinerary.title: Addis Ababa
paragraphs: Welcome to Addis Ababa! Today, we explore Ethiopia’s exciting capital city.
First, we visit the National Museum. Here, you’ll see “Lucy,” a famous skeleton that is 3.2 million years old. Lucy helps us understand where humans came from.
Next, we go to the Holy Trinity Cathedral. This is an important church with beautiful colored glass windows. Emperor Haile Selassie, a famous Ethiopian leader, is buried here.
Then, we drive up Mount Entoto. You can breathe fresh mountain air and see amazing views of the whole city.

Finally, we experience the busy Merkato Market. This is Africa’s largest outdoor market. You can buy traditional Ethiopian coffee, colorful cloth, and handmade items. It’s a great place to feel the local culture!

itinerary.title: Addis Ababa – Bahir Dar (flight)
paragraphs: In the morning, we take a flight to Bahir Dar.

After you check into your hotel, we will take a private boat on Lake Tana. We will visit the Ura Kidane Mehret Ethiopian Orthodox Church on the Zege Peninsula. This church was built in the 14th century, and the round building you see today is from the 16th century. Inside, you’ll see many old wall paintings (from 100 to 250 years ago).
After lunch, we drive to the village of Tis Isat to see the Blue Nile Falls. After our visit, we return to Bahir Dar.

itinerary.title: Bahir Dar – Gondar
paragraphs: After breakfast, we drive to Gondar, the 17th-century capital of Ethiopia. In the afternoon, we visit the Imperial Castle Compound, the Bath of Emperor Fasiladas, the Church of Quskuam Mariam, the residence of Empress Mintwab, and the Church of Debre Birhan Sillassie, famous for its wall and ceiling paintings.

itinerary.title: Gondar – Simien Mountains NP – Gondar
paragraphs: After breakfast, we drive from Gondar to Debark. Debark is the main office for the Simien Mountains National Park. Here, we get permission to enter the park and meet our local guide.

From Debark, we drive about 16 kilometers to the park gate. Then, we go another 6 kilometers to Buit Ras, which is the first area of the park. We will walk (trek) for about 3-4 hours to Chilkuwanit. This is one of the most beautiful viewpoints, with amazing views over the mountains.

You will see groups of Gelada Baboons, which are special monkeys found only in Ethiopia. You might also see jackals, klipspringers (small antelopes), and different birds. Afterward, we return to Gondar.

itinerary.title: Gondar – Simien Mountains National Park
paragraphs: After breakfast, we continue our journey to the Simien Mountains National Park. We will arrive at the highest lodge in Africa around noon.

In the afternoon, after lunch, we start exploring the Simien Mountains National Park. This park is a UNESCO World Nature Heritage site because of its special landscape and unique animals. In the park, you can get very close to the friendly Gelada Baboons.
In the late afternoon, we return to the Simien Mountains Lodge. This lodge is very comfortable and has wonderful views of the Simien mountains. We will spend the night here.

itinerary.title: Simien Mountains National Park
paragraphs: Today, we go to Sankaber (3220 meters high) to see the amazing views and Ethiopia’s deepest waterfall, called Jinbar (which means “the gate of hell”). We will take a nice walk here for about 2 hours.
We hope to see more wild animals, like the Walia Ibex (a wild goat found only here) and the Simien fox. In the late afternoon, we drive back to the lodge and spend another night.

itinerary.title: Simien Mountains National Park – Axum
paragraphs: After breakfast, we continue our drive to Axum, with more stunning views along the way. Axum is 1637 meters high and is considered a holy city in Ethiopia. Christianity started here more than 2000 years ago. The Axumite kingdom was also the beginning of Ethiopian civilization.

itinerary.title: Axum
paragraphs: Today, we’re going to explore the historic city of Axum. Our journey will take us to many amazing places. First, we’ll see the famous Axum stelae, also called obelisks. These are enormous stones that people placed there a very long time ago, and they’re the biggest single stones ever put up by humans anywhere in the world! Our tour continues at the Mariam Tsion Church, which is very special because it’s built on the exact spot where Ethiopia’s first church stood. We’ll also get to see the Palace of Queen Sheba, the home of a famous queen from history. Then, we’ll discover King Ezana’s inscriptions, which are old writings carved into stone, telling us stories from the past. Finally, we’ll visit the tombs of Kings Kaleb and Gabre Meskel, where these important kings were buried.

itinerary.title: Axum – Hawzen
paragraphs: After breakfast, we drive to Yeha. This was an old town even before Axum. It is famous for its amazing 12-meter-high stone temple, which is thought to be more than 2,500 years old.
After lunch, we continue our drive to Hawzen.

itinerary.title: Hawzen
paragraphs: After breakfast, we drive into the Gheralta Mountains. We will visit some of the amazing rock churches of Tigray, like Marian Korkor and Daniel Korkor. These are old churches built on top of rocky mountains. We will take a nice walk to the churches with unforgettable views over the Gheralta plains.

After lunch, we visit other historical churches in the area, such as Abune Yemata Guh. To reach this church, you need to climb a rock face for about 20 minutes. It’s exciting but safe! The church is built right into a high cliff. The whole climb takes about 1 hour.

itinerary.title: Hawzen – Lalibela
paragraphs: After breakfast, we drive through the Wollo mountains to Lalibela. Just before we arrive in Lalibela, we will visit the Yimrehane Christos Monastery, which is from the 11th century. We will reach Lalibela in the late afternoon.

itinerary.title: Lalibela
paragraphs: Today, we visit the 11 famous rock-hewn churches of Lalibela, also called the “8th wonder of the world.” The Lalibela churches are carved directly out of the solid rock. They are huge and seem almost impossible to build! Some are carved from one big rock, and others are connected by long underground tunnels. Some are caves that were made bigger.

The first group of six churches sits together: Bet Golgotha, Bet Mikeal, Bet Mariam, Bet Maskel, Bet Dangal, and Bet Medhanealem. Bet Medhanealem is the largest rock-hewn church in the world and looks like a Greek temple.

After lunch, we visit the second group of churches, located south of the Jordan River. This group includes Bet Giyorgis, which is possibly the most beautiful of all the Lalibela churches. Bet Giyorgis is a little separate from the others, on a sloping rock terrace. You can only reach it through a tunnel. The other four churches south of the Jordan River are Bet Emanuel, Bet Mercurios, Bet Aba Libanos, and Bet Gabriel and Rufeal. Bet Emanuel’s detailed outside has been praised by many art experts.

itinerary.title: Lalibela – Addis Ababa (flight)
paragraphs: Today, we take a flight back to Addis Ababa. Depending on the flight time, we might visit the Ne’akuto Le’ab Monastery just outside of town.
When you arrive at Bole International Airport in Addis Ababa, you will be taken to your hotel. If you are interested, there are many places to see and shop.

In the evening, you will enjoy a special farewell dinner at one of Addis Ababa’s traditional restaurants. You’ll experience cultural songs, dances, and traditional Ethiopian food and drinks. Afterward, you will be taken to Bole International Airport for your departure, or to your hotel if you are staying longer in Ethiopia.

title: 8 Days Omo Valley
teaser: The Dorze, Konso, Hamar, Karo and Mursi — eight days among the peoples of Ethiopia’s far south.
overview: Ethiopia’s is rich diverse ethnographic attractions attributed to its nations, nationalities, and peoples of more than 83 languages and 200 dialects. One of the most important locations for these ethnographic tourism attractions is the lower Omo Valley of Southern Ethiopia which is home to an astonishing mix of small, contrasting ethnic groups such as Gnangatom, Karo, Dassench, Bodi, Mursi, Surma, Arbore, and Hamer – some of the most fascinating people and cultures. A trip through Ethiopia that focuses on the South of the country, inhabited by some of the most attractions of the country: the Dorze with their spectacular huts, the Konso, the Mursi warriors whose women wear the lip plate, the Karos with their body paints and the Hamers with their peculiar clothing and beautiful women who cover their bodies and hair with grease and reddish mud. An ethnic journey, designed to be able to contact the great human wealth that this part of Ethiopia.
highlights: Encounter the diverse tribes of the Omo Valley.
Experience the daily life of the Hamer, Mursi, Karo, and other indigenous communities.
Learn about their fascinating cultures.
Witness the vibrant and colorful weekly markets

itinerary.title: Addis Ababa
paragraphs: Arrival Bole International Airport and transfer to your hotel. After breakfast you will start your city tour of Addis Ababa with the National Museum of Ethiopia. This is one of the best museums in quality and diversity of the exhibits. Archeological exhibits include the 3.2 million-year-old fossil of Lucy (or Dinkinesh – ‘thou art wonderful’- in the native language), a hominoid woman of the specious of Australopithecus Afarensis. The discovery of Lucy’s fossil in 1974 forced a complete rethink of human genealogy, providing that our ancestors were walking 2.5 million years earlier than had been supposed.

itinerary.title: Addis Ababa – Arba Minch (flight)
paragraphs: Morning at 8am arrive bole International Airport. After breakfast and after a few hours rest we will take the afternoon flight to fly Arba Minch. After we arrive Arba Minch meet the driver and drive along a very scenic route to the mountain village of Chencha, home of the Dorze people. Renowned for their cotton weaving, called Shammas. And their distinctive house- towering beehive shaped structures made from woven thatch. Visit and proceed to Arba Minch.

itinerary.title: Arba Minch – Jinka
paragraphs: Leaving Arba Minch, we drive southwards to Jinka. You visit the Konso village who live in a land of low terraced hills. They are reputed to be the hardest workers in the country. Their elaborately terraced hillside grows some of the country’s best coffee. They have an artistic tradition and erect peculiar totems on the grave of their deceased. We experience interesting cultural encounters meeting with different tribes along the way. These tribes include the Ari, Benna and Tsemay.

itinerary.title: Jinka – Mago – Turmi
paragraphs: After breakfast, take a day excursion to Mago National Park to visit the Mursi village. The Mursi are one of the most original ethnic groups. They live in very low huts made of straw leaves. The women like to wear terra cotta on their enormously stretched lower lips and ear lobes. The men are famous for their hairstyle. Back to Jinka and stop for lunch. After lunch we proceed drive to Turmi.

itinerary.title: Turmi – Omorate – Karo – Turmi
paragraphs: This day you will take an excursion to Omorate where you will have cultural experience with the Geleb/ Dassenech people inhabitants of lower Omo River Valley. Visit and drive back to Turmi. In the afternoon we drive to karo village.

itinerary.title: Turmi – Arba Minch
paragraphs: On this day after breakfast e drive back to Arba Minch. On the way visit the Erbore tribe.

itinerary.title: Arba Minch – Hawassa
paragraphs: After early breakfast we take a boat cruise on Lake Chamo. At the spot called “Azo Gebeya” or ‘crocodile market’, huge concentration of crocodiles, herds of hippo as well as many species of birds can be observed. After visit the crocodile market we drive to Hawassa.

itinerary.title: Hawassa – Addis Ababa
paragraphs: After breakfast we drive back to Addis Ababa. On the way visit the Abjatta Shalla national park to see some birds and mammals. In the evening a farewell dinner at one of the best traditional restaurant in Addis to see different types of cultural music and dance with a traditional Ethiopian foods.

itinerary.title: Addis Ababa
paragraphs: The group members will be arriving at different times throughout the day from various international destinations. Since their flights are not synchronized, we will coordinate their arrivals accordingly. If, however, everyone arrives in Addis Ababa (Bole International Airport) around the same time or from the same origin, we can organize a short city tour or sightseeing activity while waiting for the rest of the group. For those arriving much earlier or later, we will arrange airport transfers and accommodations as planned. Please share your flight details in advance so we can optimize the schedule.

itinerary.title: Addis Ababa
paragraphs: Begin your Addis Ababa sightseeing with a scenic drive north to Mount Entoto, offering breathtaking views from its 3200m peak. Descending, you’ll visit the Ethnographic Museum, showcasing a comprehensive array of Ethiopian crafts and historically significant items. The National Museum awaits with its remarkable archaeological finds, including the iconic 3.4-million-year-old ‘Lucy’ fossil. After lunch, explore the grandeur of Trinity Cathedral, the largest and most revered church in Addis Ababa, built in 1941 and notable for its art and architecture. Your tour culminates with a drive through Merkato, Africa’s largest open-air market, a bustling hub of trade and local life.

itinerary.title: Addis Ababa – Arba Minch (flight)
paragraphs: Begin your day with an early breakfast before transferring to the airport to catch your morning flight to Arba Minch. Upon arrival, our drivers will take you to your accommodation. In the afternoon, visit the Dorze Village, renowned for its unique cultural traditions. The Dorze people are celebrated for their exceptional weaving craftsmanship, a skill passed down through generations. Other distinctive practices include producing local liquors, playing traditional music, and crafting food from the false banana plant (kocho). The Dorze community, who reside on lush hillsides, are also famous for their towering beehive-shaped huts—a remarkable architectural feat that reflects their ingenuity.

itinerary.title: Arba Minch – Turmi
paragraphs: This morning, after having early breakfast we take a boat cruise across the waters of Lake Chamo. Our destination is the renowned “Azo Gebeya,” or ‘crocodile market,’ a truly spectacular sight where an impressive number of large crocodiles gather. Keep your cameras ready for glimpses of wallowing hippos and the diverse and colorful birdlife that thrives in this ecosystem. Later, our overland journey southwards leads us towards Turmi. Our exploration includes a visit to a traditional Konso village, nestled within a striking landscape of gently sloping, terraced hills, recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage site. The Konso people are widely respected for their diligent nature, evident in the meticulously crafted terraces that carpet their hillsides, surprisingly producing some of the country’s most exceptional coffee. Their ancient artistic heritage is manifested in the distinctive totems that mark the final resting places of their ancestors. As we travel, we look forward to fascinating cultural exchanges, encountering the unique customs and traditions of the various tribes that inhabit this captivating region.

itinerary.title: Turmi – Omorate – Turmi
paragraphs: On this day after breakfast, our day unfolds with an excursion to Omorate, where we’ll have the privilege of meeting the Dassanech people – often called the ‘people of the Delta’ – who make their home along the northern shores of the vast Lake Turkana. After our visit, we’ll journey back to Turmi. The afternoon brings an encounter with the captivating Hamar people in their village. Renowned as one of the most striking and proud communities in the Omo Valley, the Hamar truly embody a sense of beauty and grace. Their women are particularly eye-catching, adorned in elegant leather skirts embellished with delicate, tiny pearls. Intricate and elaborate hairstyles serve as another significant form of their personal expression and beauty.

itinerary.title: Turmi – Nyangatom/Karo – Turmi
paragraphs: Begin your day with an early departure from Turmi, heading toward the remote village of Kangatan. From there, take a guided walk through lush fields, where locals tend to their crops, before arriving at a traditional Nyangatom tribal village. Immerse yourself in their vibrant culture, learning about their unique customs, intricate beadwork, and pastoral way of life.

After the visit, journey back across the river and continue to the spectacular Karo village of Korcho, perched dramatically on a Cliffside with breathtaking views over the Omo River. The Karo people, though the smallest tribe in the Omo Valley, are renowned for their stunning body paintings and elaborate scarification, making them some of the most visually striking communities in the region. Spend time interacting with the villagers, capturing their artistry, and admiring their striking traditional adornments.
Afterwards, we will enjoy a scenic drive back to Turmi, reflecting on the unforgettable cultural encounters of the day.

itinerary.title: Turmi – Jinka
paragraphs: After breakfast, drive to Jinka, stopping at Dimeka, home to one of Ethiopia’s most vibrant weekly markets (Tuesdays & Saturdays). Here, you’ll see the Hamer, Benna, Tsemai, Ari, and Karo tribes trading goods, dressed in traditional attire. Soak in the lively atmosphere before continuing through scenic landscapes to Jinka, the cultural heart of the Omo Valley.

itinerary.title: Jinka – Bodi/Mursi – Jinka
paragraphs: We’ll wake up early drive towards Mago National Park, a wild and beautiful area home to some of Ethiopia’s most iconic tribes. Our focus today is meeting the Bodi (known for their honey-colored body paint and unique ceremonies) and the Mursi (famous for their striking lip plates and decorative scarifications). These tribes have preserved their ancient customs in remarkable ways, and visiting their villages gives us a rare glimpse into traditions that have remained unchanged for generations. The drive itself is an adventure, with scenic landscapes and possible wildlife sightings along the way! After a visit drive back to Jinka.

itinerary.title: Jinka – Addis Ababa (flight)
paragraphs: On this day after breakfast we take the morning flight back to Addis Ababa. We should be in the airport before one and half hours for check in. In the afternoon relax in the hotel. In the evening a farewell dinner at one of the best traditional restaurant in Addis to see different types of cultural music and dance with a traditional Ethiopian foods.

itinerary.title: Addis Ababa – Lalibela (flight)
paragraphs: After breakfast, take a short flight to Lalibela. After checking in at the hotel, visit the rock-hewn Churches of Lalibela. Lalibela is the jewel in the crown of Ethiopia, home to the most famous churches and the scene of many major religious ceremonies. Also known as ‘Africa’s Petra’, Lalibela and its rock-hewn churches are among Ethiopia’s top attractions. Visit the churches: Bete Medhane Alem, Bete Mariam, Bete Maskal, Bete Danaghel, Bete Golgotha & Bete Mikael, and Bete Giorgis. In the afternoon, visit the remaining churches: Bete Amanuel, Bete Markorios, Bete Aba Libanos, and Bete Gebriel-Rufael.

itinerary.title: Lalibela
paragraphs: After breakfast, visit the rest of the rock-hewn churches of Lalibela and take an excursion to visit some of the churches outside Lalibela town.

itinerary.title: Lalibela – Addis Ababa (flight)
paragraphs: Take a morning flight back to Addis Ababa, where you can enjoy some last-minute shopping or sightseeing before your departure.
End of the Journey

title: 3 Days Harar
teaser: Ninety-nine mosques, five ancient gates and the nightly feeding of the hyenas in Islam’s fourth holy city.
overview: The fortified historic town of Harar is located in the eastern part of the country on a plateau with deep gorges surrounded by deserts and savannah. The walls surrounding this sacred Muslim city were built between the 13th and 16th centuries. Harar Jugol, said to be the fourth holiest city of Islam, numbers 82 mosques, three of which date from the 10th century, and 102 shrines, but the townhouses with their exceptional interior design constitute the most spectacular part of Harar’s cultural heritage. The impact of African and Islamic traditions on the development of the town’s building types and urban layout make for its particular character and uniqueness.

title: 6 Days Danakil Desert Expedition
teaser: Erta Ale’s lava lake, the salt caravans and sulphur springs of Dallol — one of the most extraordinary landscapes on earth.
overview: The Danakil Depression is the northernmost part of the Afar Depression that is also known as the Afar Triangle. The Afar Triangle is a geological depression that sits on what is known as the Afar Triple Junction which is part of the Great Rift Valley. The Afar Triple Junction is at the crossroads of three nations that include Eritrea to the north, Djibouti to the west and, to the south, the entire Afar Region in northern Ethiopia. Within the Danakil Depression are two active volcanoes. Mount Ayalu is the westernmost and older of the two volcanoes. It sits at the southern end of the Danakil Depression. The other active volcano is known as Erta Ale. It is amongst several crater lakes bubbling molten rock from the earth’s core. Within the Danakil Depression is Dallol, which is today the hottest place on earth that is inhabited by human beings. Average temperatures are as high as 35 degrees Celsius.
highlights: Erta Ale, an active volcano.
Dallol, the unique dramatic and colorful geological formations.
Lake Asale, where bricks of salt are cut from the lake and loaded onto camel caravans.

Descending down to Addis, proceed to the Ethnographic museum, which displays a very large collection of Ethiopian crafts and items of historical interest. Continue to visit the Trinity Cathedral, the highest ranking Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo cathedral in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. This was built in 1941 to commemorate the Ethiopian victory over Italian occupation and is an important place of worship in Ethiopia. After lunch, proceed to the National museum that houses the 3.2 million years old fossils of ‘Lucy’ (perhaps our earliest ancestor) is among other interesting archeological findings.

itinerary.title: Hamed Ela – Lake Asale and Dallol
paragraphs: Drive to the Salt Lake Asale, and visit the salt workers and the merchant from the highland and proceed to Dallol and enjoy the spectacular view and small hill which is colorful by hot spring in several places. The hot spring out with the sulfurs, potash, and salt it forms spectacular formation. Drive back to Ahmed Ela.

itinerary.title: Hamed Ela – Erta Ale
paragraphs: Morning, start driving on a rough road to a small village called Kusrawad, to get permission and militias for an access to Erta Ale. The name Erta Ale means ‘Smoking Mountain’ by the local Afar language, it is one of the oldest lava lake in the world, Erta-Ale range is located to the southeast of the summit and is bounded by curvilinear fault scarps on the southeast side. Fresh-looking basaltic lava flows from these fissures have poured into the caldera and locally overflowed its rim. The major recorded eruption was on 1907, and there were other continuous eruptions. To access the summit 3-4hours walk on to the lava field.
