title: 11 Days Bale Mountains & Omo Valley
teaser: Ethiopian wolves and mountain nyala on the Sanetti Plateau, then south to the peoples of the Omo Valley.
overview: Ethiopia’s most important biodiversity hotspot, Bale Mountains National Park UNESCO world heritage sites supports a rich mosaic of high-altitude habitats including lush evergreen forest, stands of giant bamboo, pastel-shaded moorland, and sheltered river valleys swathed in fragrant juniper-hagenia woodland. The park is the most important stronghold to three endemic large mammal species – the charismatic Ethiopian wolf, handsome mountain nyala, and delightful Bale monkey – while its incredible avifauna is reflected by the African Birding Club having listed it as one of the continent’s top five birding hotspots. South Omo Valley a vast semi-arid region flanking the lower Omo River before it flows across the border into Kenya’s Lake Turkana – is home to some of the continent’s most staunchly traditional animist ethnic groups. In many respects, this remote region comes across as a kind of living museum, supporting around two dozen different tribes, some numbering tens of thousands, others a few hundred. Several of the tribes place great cultural emphasis on body ornamentation – ranging from the large clay lip plates worn by the Mursi women, to the more widespread customs of ritual scarification, body painting and henna-dyed hair.
highlights: Explore the diverse ecosystems of the Bale Mountains.
Witness the rare and endangered Ethiopian wolf in its natural habitat.
Enjoy breathtaking views of the Ethiopian highlands.
Encounter the diverse tribes of the Omo Valley.
Experience the daily life of the Hamer, Mursi, Karo, and other indigenous communities.
Learn about their fascinating cultures.
Witness the vibrant and colorful weekly markets.

itinerary.title: Addis Ababa
paragraphs: Arrival Bole International Airport and transfer to your hotel.

itinerary.title: Addis Ababa
paragraphs: After breakfast you will start your city tour of Addis Ababa with the National Museum of Ethiopia. This is one of the best museums in quality and diversity of the exhibits. Archeological exhibits include the 3.2 million-year-old fossil of Lucy (or Dinkinesh – ‘thou art wonderful’- in the native language), a hominoid woman of the specious of Australopithecus Afarensis. The discovery of Lucy’s fossil in 1974 forced a complete rethink of human genealogy, providing that our ancestors were walking 2.5 million years earlier than had been supposed.

itinerary.title: Addis Ababa – Goba (Bale Mountains NP)
paragraphs: Morning driving from Addis to the Bale Mountains National Park. Arrive at the park headquarters in the afternoon. Meet with guides and drive to the Gaysey Grasslands. Take a leisurely afternoon hike, possibly spotting two endemic mammals that frequent the area: Menelik’s Bushbuck and the Mountain Nyala. Birds in this area include the Blue-Winged Goose, the Spot-Breasted Lapwing, the Abyssinian Long Claw, the Wattled Ibis, the Black-Headed Siskin, Rouget’s Rail, and numerous other species. Then drive to Goba.

itinerary.title: Excursion to Sanetti
paragraphs: Today you will have an excursion to Sanetti Plateau, the highest plateau in Africa. Here you may encounter the endemics of Ethiopia Wolf. Visit and proceed to Harrena Forest, the second dense forest in Ethiopia.

itinerary.title: Goba – Arba Minch
paragraphs: On this day after breakfast drive to Arba Minch.

itinerary.title: Arba Minch
paragraphs: In the morning, we will have a boat cruise on Lake Chamo to see some of the biggest African crocodiles. Hippopotamuses and many beautiful aquatic birds including the lovely Kingfisher and African Fish Eagle are also easily seen. In the afternoon, visit the Dorze village. The Dorzes are famed for their amazing weaving mastery. Weaving, producing local liquors, music, and false banana food (kocho) production are some of the unique traits of the Dorze people. Dorze people live on hills and they are famous for their huge huts, resembling a giant beehive.

itinerary.title: Arba Minch – Turmi
paragraphs: In the morning after breakfast drive to Turmi via the villages of Konso, home to the Konso people, designated as a UNESCO World Heritage site. A highland people, the Konso are known for the ancient and intricate terraces that encircle their well-planned villages. Each Konso village begins on a hill top. As the population grows a new “ring” of homes are built around the hilltop. When the final “ring” reaches near the bottom of the hill, a new village on a different hill must be built. Look for the “generation pole” located in each village. Every 18 years and new pole is added to the others making it easy to calculate the age of the village. After having lunch in Konso, proceed to Turmi, home of the Hamer tribe. In the evening, you might be lucky to see the traditional night dancing of the Hamer people, known as evangadi, if there will be a wedding ceremony. If there is no the opportunity to see and participate the Hamer tribe wedding ceremony visit the Hamer village.

itinerary.title: Turmi
paragraphs: In the morning we drive to another Omo Valley Tribes known as Nyangatom then after visiting the villages of those tribes we will drive to another village to visit the Karo Tribes which is lying on the river side of Omo later we will be driving to the town of Turmi for overnight.

itinerary.title: Turmi – Jinka
paragraphs: After breakfast drive to Jinka, via Dimeka and Key Afar. Tuesdays and Saturdays are market days in Dimeka, which are among of the most colorful markets in the area. In this market you can find tribes such as Tsemai, Benna, Hamer, Karo and Ari. Afterwards, continue to Jinka.

itinerary.title: Jinka
paragraphs: In early morning drive to in the village of Bodi tribe. The Bodi tribe has a unique tradition of body modification where they practice scarification. The process involves making small cuts on the body and then rubbing ash into the wounds, which leaves permanent scars. The scars are believed to represent beauty and are seen as a sign of strength and endurance. Men on the other hand, are very plump, with big bellies. The fatter a man is, the more attractive he is to women. After a visit drive to the village of Mursi. The Mursi are Known for their lip plate tradition; an unmarried woman’s lower lip will be pierced and then progressively stretched over the period of a year. A clay disc indented like a pulley wheel is squeezed into the hole in the lip.

itinerary.title: Jinka – Addis Ababa (flight)
paragraphs: On this day after breakfast we take the morning flight back to Addis Ababa. We should be in the airport before one and half hours for check in. After we arrive in Addis Ababa having a relaxing lunch and take you to a visit of the Ethnographic Museum. The Ethnological Museum, Addis Ababa, in Ethiopia, is a public institution dedicated to ethnology and culture. The Ethnological Museum houses anthropological, musicological and cultural objects. The Ethnological Museum is the first university museum in Ethiopia. In the evening a farewell dinner at one of the best traditional restaurant in Addis to see different types of cultural music and dance with a traditional Ethiopian foods.

title: 13 Days Historic North & Cultural South
teaser: Lalibela, Gondar and Lake Tana in the north; the Dorze, Konso and Omo Valley peoples in the south.
overview: This exciting Ethiopian adventure begins in Addis Ababa, where you’ll explore the capital’s vibrant markets and historical sites before flying to Bahir Dar to discover ancient island monasteries on Lake Tana and the majestic Blue Nile Falls. Next, you’ll travel to Gondar, often called the “Camelot of Africa,” to marvel at its royal castles and embark on a breathtaking day trip to the Simien Mountains National Park, home to unique wildlife and stunning landscapes. A flight then takes you to Lalibela to witness the incredible rock-hewn churches before returning to Addis Ababa. The journey then shifts south to the Omo Valley, flying to Jinka as your base. Here, you’ll immerse yourself in the rich cultures of various indigenous tribes, including the Mursi, Hamer, Dassanech, Nyangatom, and Karo people, experiencing their unique traditions and way of life before flying back to Addis Ababa for some last-minute shopping and a farewell dinner.
highlights: Explore the vibrant capital, including the National Museum and Mercato.
Discover ancient island monasteries on Lake Tana and visit the Blue Nile Falls.
Marvel at royal castles and take a breathtaking day trip to Simien Mountains National Park.
Immerse yourself in the unique cultures of various indigenous tribes like the Mursi, Hamer, Dassanech, Nyangatom, and Karo.

itinerary.title: Addis Ababa
paragraphs: Welcome to Addis Ababa! Today is all about settling in and getting a taste of Ethiopia’s bustling capital. You’ll likely arrive at Bole International Airport and transfer to your hotel. Depending on your arrival time, you might have the afternoon free to relax, or perhaps you’d like to dive straight into exploring some of the city’s highlights. A visit to the National Museum, home to “Lucy,” our ancient ancestor, is a popular choice, offering a fascinating glimpse into human origins. Afterwards, you could wander through the Mercato, one of Africa’s largest open-air markets, to experience the vibrant local life and perhaps pick up some souvenirs. The day will conclude with dinner, enjoying some delicious Ethiopian cuisine.

itinerary.title: Addis Ababa – Bahir Dar (flight)
paragraphs: This morning, you’ll transfer to Bole International Airport for a domestic flight to Bahir Dar, a picturesque city located on the shores of Lake Tana, Ethiopia’s largest lake. Upon arrival, you’ll check into your hotel and then embark on a relaxing boat trip on Lake Tana. This is a wonderful opportunity to visit some of the ancient island monasteries, adorned with stunning frescoes and housing invaluable religious artifacts. As you cruise across the lake, you’ll also have a chance to observe local fishermen in their traditional papyrus boats. In the afternoon drive to Tia Abay to visit the blue Nile falls.

itinerary.title: Bahir Dar – Gondar
paragraphs: Today, after breakfast the journey north towards Gondar, often referred to as the “Camelot of Africa.” The drive itself offers scenic views of the Ethiopian countryside. Upon arrival in Gondar, you’ll be transported back in time as you explore the Royal Enclosure, a UNESCO World Heritage site. Here, you’ll discover impressive 17th-century castles and palaces built by various emperors, showcasing a unique blend of Ethiopian, European, and Arabian architectural styles. Don’t miss a visit to the beautifully decorated Debre Berhan Selassie Church, renowned for its ceiling adorned with winged angels.

itinerary.title: Gondar – Simien Mountains – Gondar
paragraphs: Prepare for an exciting day trip to the majestic Simien Mountains National Park, another UNESCO World Heritage site and a true natural wonder. This morning, you’ll drive from Gondar to the park, where you’ll be greeted by breathtaking landscapes of dramatic peaks, deep valleys, and jagged escarpments. You’ll embark on a rewarding trek, offering incredible opportunities to spot unique wildlife, most notably the Gelada baboons, often seen grazing on the grass. The stunning vistas and fresh mountain air make for an unforgettable experience before you return to Gondar in the late afternoon.

itinerary.title: Gondar – Lalibela (flight)
paragraphs: This morning, you’ll head back to the airport for a short flight to Lalibela, a remote town famous for its extraordinary rock-hewn churches. Upon arrival, you’ll be captivated by the sheer ingenuity and spiritual significance of these monolithic structures, carved directly out of living rock in the 12th century. You’ll spend the afternoon exploring the first group of churches, which are truly architectural marvels and an enduring testament to faith. The intricate details and the sense of awe these ancient sites inspire are truly remarkable.

itinerary.title: Lalibela – Addis Ababa
paragraphs: Today, you’ll continue your exploration of Lalibela’s incredible rock-hewn churches, visiting the remaining groups, including the iconic Bet Giyorgis (Church of St. George), a perfectly cruciform structure that seems to emerge from the earth. You’ll have time to fully appreciate the unique spiritual atmosphere and the incredible craftsmanship. In the afternoon, you’ll transfer to the airport for your flight back to Addis Ababa, reflecting on the profound history and devotion you witnessed in Lalibela.

itinerary.title: Addis Ababa – Jinka (flight)
paragraphs: This morning marks the beginning of your adventure into the Omo Valley, a region renowned for its diverse indigenous communities. You’ll take a domestic flight from Addis Ababa to Jinka, the main town in the South Omo Zone. Upon arrival, you’ll check into your accommodation and then have some time to relax or explore Jinka town, perhaps visiting the South Omo Museum & Research Centre to gain a better understanding of the local cultures you’ll encounter in the coming days.

itinerary.title: Jinka – Mago – Jinka
paragraphs: Today, you’ll embark on a fascinating excursion to Mago National Park, a protected area in the Omo Valley. The primary reason for this visit is to interact with the Mursi people, known for their distinctive lip plates worn by the women. You’ll drive through the park, observing the natural landscape, before reaching a Mursi village. This provides a unique opportunity to learn about their traditions, way of life, and artistic expressions. Remember to approach interactions with respect and sensitivity. After a rich cultural exchange, you’ll return to Jinka in the afternoon.

itinerary.title: Jinka – Turmi
paragraphs: Today’s journey takes you deeper into the Omo Valley as you drive from Jinka to Turmi, a town that serves as a gateway to the Hamer, Karo, and Nyangatom tribes. The drive itself is scenic, passing through various landscapes and offering glimpses of rural life. Upon arrival in Turmi, you’ll check into your lodge, which often blends with the natural surroundings. In the late afternoon, you might have the opportunity to visit a local Hamer village, renowned for their intricate hairstyles, body adornments, and fascinating cultural ceremonies, such as the bull jumping ritual (if circumstances allow).

itinerary.title: Turmi – Omorate – Turmi
paragraphs: This morning, you’ll head south from Turmi to Omorate, located on the banks of the Omo River. Here, you’ll cross the river by local canoe to visit a Dassanech village. The Dassanech are one of the most southerly Omo Valley tribes, and you’ll have the chance to observe their unique customs and daily routines. The experience of crossing the river and engaging with this community offers a different perspective on the diverse cultures of the region. You’ll return to Turmi in the afternoon, with time to relax or perhaps explore more of the local surroundings.

itinerary.title: Turmi – Nyangatom/Karo – Turmi
paragraphs: Today offers an opportunity to explore more of the fascinating tribes around Turmi. Depending on local market days and accessibility, you’ll either visit a Nyangatom village or a Karo village. The Nyangatom are known for their elaborate beadwork and scarification, while the Karo are famous for their intricate body painting. Both experiences offer a chance to witness traditional lifestyles and unique artistic expressions. The interactions will be respectful and insightful, providing a deeper understanding of the Omo Valley’s rich cultural tapestry. You’ll return to Turmi by the end of the day.

itinerary.title: Turmi – Jinka
paragraphs: After a memorable exploration of the Lower Omo Valley, you’ll begin your journey back north today, driving from Turmi to Jinka. This allows for a more relaxed pace and potentially a stop at a local market or a scenic viewpoint along the way. Upon arrival in Jinka, you’ll check into your hotel and have the rest of the day to relax or revisit any local spots of interest.

itinerary.title: Jinka – Addis Ababa (flight)
paragraphs: This morning, you’ll take your flight back to Addis Ababa, bringing your incredible journey through Ethiopia to a close. Upon arrival in the capital, you’ll have the opportunity for some last-minute souvenir shopping, perhaps at the local craft shops or markets. In the evening, you’ll enjoy a farewell traditional dinner, complete with delicious Ethiopian cuisine and cultural performances, a perfect way to reflect on your amazing experiences.

title: 15 Days Best of Ethiopia
teaser: Our signature journey: Addis Ababa, Lake Tana, Gondar, Lalibela, then south by Lake Chamo to the Omo Valley.
overview: This tour is an unforgettable journey through Ethiopia, a land of ancient history, stunning landscapes, and vibrant cultures. Your trip begins in Addis Ababa, where you’ll explore historic sites, museums, and bustling markets. From there, fly to Bahir Dar to discover the serene beauty of Lake Tana and the Blue Nile Falls. Continue to Gondar, home to majestic castles and churches, before traveling to the breathtaking rock-hewn churches of Lalibela.

Venture south to Arba Minch, where you’ll cruise Lake Chamo and meet the Dorze people, known for their unique woven houses. Dive deeper into Ethiopia’s rich cultural tapestry as you visit the tribes of the Omo Valley, including the Mursi, Hamer, and Dassanech people, each with their own fascinating traditions.

Your adventure ends back in Addis Ababa, where you’ll enjoy a farewell dinner with traditional music and dance. This journey offers a perfect mix of history, nature, and cultural encounters, leaving you with memories to last a lifetime.
highlights: Explore Addis Ababa’s historic sites, including Mount Entoto and the National Museum.
Discover the ancient rock-hewn churches of Lalibela, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Cruise Lake Tana and visit the Blue Nile Falls in Bahir Dar.
Step into Ethiopia’s royal past in Gondar with its stunning castles.
Meet the vibrant tribes of the Omo Valley, like the Mursi and Hamer people.
Enjoy a scenic boat ride on Lake Chamo and see crocodiles & hippos up close.

itinerary.title: Addis Ababa
paragraphs: Be welcomed at Addis Ababa Bole international airport and transfer to hotel.

itinerary.title: Addis Ababa
paragraphs: Begin your sightseeing of Addis with a drive up north to Mount Entoto. The panorama from the peak (3,200 m) is breathtaking. Descending down to Addis, proceed to the Ethnographic museum, which displays a very large collection of Ethiopian crafts and items of historical interest. The National museum that houses the 3.4 million years old fossils of ‘Lucy’ (perhaps our earliest ancestor) is among other interesting archeological findings. After lunch, visit the Trinity Cathedral, the largest and most revered of all the churches, which was built in 1941. To wrap up, drive through the largest open-air market in Africa.

itinerary.title: Addis Ababa – Bahir Dar (flight)
paragraphs: Fly to Bahir Dar. You will be met upon arrival and after checking-in your hotel, on this day you take a boat cruise on Lake Tana to visit the 14th century Monastery of Ura Kidane Mihret which is the most famous of the Zege peninsula monasteries with a very beautiful painted maqdas and priceless collection of crosses as well as crowns. Afternoon, you will drive to the village of Tis Isat to see the Blue Nile falls (please be informed that due to the newly constructed electric dam in the vicinity the water level of the falls could be very minimal).

itinerary.title: Bahir Dar – Gondar
paragraphs: After breakfast drive to Gondar through the spectacular route around Lake Tana. Gondar is a town founded in 1636 by the great Emperor Fassiladas. Set in a landscape of incomparable beauty, it was the Royal Capital of Ethiopia. Visit the Castles and Churches built by Emperor Fassiladas and his descendants. Later proceed to the fascinating Debre Birhan Selassie Church its walls and ceilings decorated with scenes of Biblical lore and medieval history.

itinerary.title: Gondar – Lalibela
paragraphs: Drive to Lalibela via Gashena with watching countryside people & variety highland landscapes.

itinerary.title: Lalibela
paragraphs: Lalibela is the jewel in the crown of Ethiopia, the home of the most famous churches and the scene of so many major religious ceremonies. Also known, as ‘Africa’s petra’, Lalibela and its rock-hewn Churches are arguably Ethiopia’s top most attractions. Visit the rock-hewn Churches. These Churches include Bete Medhane Alem, Bete Mariam, Bete Maskal, Bete Danaghel, Bete Golgotha & Bete Mikael, and Bete Giorgis.
Afternoon, you will visit the rest of the rock hewn churches of Lalibela like Bete Amanuel, Bete Markorios, Bete Aba Libanos, and Bete Gebriel-Rufael.

itinerary.title: Lalibela – Addis Ababa (flight)
paragraphs: Transfer to Lalibela airport and fly to Addis Ababa. Be met upon arrival and transfer to your hotel for refreshment, evening, have a farewell dinner party at one of the best traditional restaurant where you will see the folkloric dances of the people of Ethiopia, and taste the variety of Ethiopian meals. Overnight Eliana Hotel.

itinerary.title: Addis Ababa – Arba Minch
paragraphs: Morning, drive to the town of Arba Minch, along a very scenic route to the mountain village of Chencha, home of the Dorze people. Renowned for their cotton weaving, called Shamma and their distinctive house- towering beehive shaped structures made from woven thatch. Visit and proceed to Arba Minch.

itinerary.title: Arba Minch
paragraphs: The Nech Sar Park has a beautiful setting sandwiched between Lakes: Chamo and Abaya. Nech Sar meaning white grass, is derived from the plain where the color of the grass is golden white. The park abounds as well a great diversity of plant and bird life. Take a boat cruise on Lake Chamo. At the spot called “Azo Gebeya” or ‘crocodile market’, huge concentration of crocodiles, herds of hippo as well as many species of birds can be observed.

itinerary.title: Arba Minch – Jinka
paragraphs: Leaving Arba Minch, we drive southwards to Jinka. You visit the Konso village who live in a land of low terraced hills. They are reputed to be the hardest workers in the country. Their elaborately terraced hillside grows some of the country’s best coffee. They have an artistic tradition and erect peculiar totems on the grave of their deceased. We experience interesting cultural encounters meeting with different tribes along the way.

itinerary.title: Jinka – Mursi – Turmi
paragraphs: This day you will have an excursion to Mago National Park to visit the Mursi village. The Mursi are one of the most original ethnic groups. They live in very low huts made of straw leaves. The women like to wear terra-cotta on their enormously stretched lower lips and ear lobes. The men are famous for their hair style. Visit and drive back to Jinka for lunch. Then proceed to Turmi where the Hamar people live.

itinerary.title: Turmi – Omorate – Turmi (140kms)
paragraphs: After having your breakfast, you will have an excursion to Omorate to visit the Dassanech people ‘people of the Delta’, who lives on the northern shore of Lake Turkana. Visit and drive back to Turmi. In the afternoon you will visit the Hamar village. The Hamar are one of the most beautiful and dignified people in the Omo basin. The women wear elegant leather skirts festooned with tiny pearls. Elaborate hairstyles are another form of personal adornment.

itinerary.title: Turmi – Arba Minch
paragraphs: After Breakfast we drive back to Arba Minch, enroute we will visit Erbore and Tsemay tribes.

itinerary.title: Arba Minch – Addis Ababa
paragraphs: Today you will drive back to Addis visiting en route Tiya Stelae, declared a world heritage by UNESCO, one of eight such sites in the country. It highlights the widespread presence of mysterious engraved stelae stretching across this region of southern Ethiopia.

itinerary.title: Addis Ababa
paragraphs: On this day after breakfast we will do something you want to do in Addis, then at night transfer to airport for your flight back to home.

Blue Nile falls and Lake Tana Monasteries

History, Nature and Culture

paragraphs: In the morning we take the morning flight to Bahir Dar. The most attractive church in the Lake Tana region founded in the 14th century although the present circular church dates from the 16th century. Its interior is decorated with numerous murals painted between 100 and 250 years ago. The church has its treasury in a nearby outbuilding, which contains the richly embroidered robes of Negus Tekle Haymanot and his wife Laqetch Gegre Mehdin, as well as the crowns of Emperor Yohannes IV, Emperor Tewodros II, Negus Tekle Haymanot, and Emperor Tekle Giyorgis. Then travel to see hippos at the mouth of the Blue Nile River. Keep your eyes open for the spectacular birdlife. After lunch drive to Blue Nile falls (Tis Abay) meaning in Amharic is “great smoke”. The falls are one of the best – known tourist destinations.

title: Genna: Ethiopian Christmas in Lalibela
teaser: Candlelit vigils and white-robed pilgrims among the rock churches of Lalibela on Ethiopian Christmas Eve.
overview: This captivating Ethiopian journey blends ancient history, breathtaking landscapes, and vibrant cultural traditions. Explore Addis Ababa’s rich heritage through its museums and cathedrals, then venture to Bahir Dar to discover Lake Tana’s island monasteries and the thunderous Blue Nile Falls. The medieval castles of Gondar and the stunning Debre Birhan Selassie Church transport you back in time, while the Simien Mountains offer dramatic trekking among endemic Gelada Baboons and sweeping vistas. The spiritual heart of the journey lies in Lalibela, where you’ll witness the magic of Ethiopian Christmas (Genna) amid candlelit processions, rock-hewn churches, and joyful celebrations.

From bustling cities to serene highlands, this itinerary immerses you in Ethiopia’s diverse wonders. Glide across Lake Tana’s tranquil waters, hike to roaring waterfalls, and marvel at UNESCO-listed castles and churches adorned with vivid religious art. The Simien Mountains deliver awe-inspiring nature, while Lalibela’s living traditions, especially during Genna, create unforgettable moments of connection. The adventure culminates in Addis Ababa with a festive farewell of traditional cuisine, music, and dance, leaving you with lasting memories of Ethiopia’s warmth and grandeur.

Embark on a boat trip to visit the fascinating monasteries on the lake’s islands

“Camelot of Africa,” Gondar, with its well-preserved 17th-century castles and palaces

itinerary.title: Addis Ababa – Bahir Dar (flight)
paragraphs: After early breakfast drive to Airport to take a short and comfortable flight to Bahir Dar, a vibrant green city beautifully set on the shores of Lake Tana. Ethiopia’s largest and most picturesque lake. Here, you’ll embark on a peaceful boat journey across the lake’s calm, sparkling waters. Your first stop is the historic Ura Kidane Mihret Monastery, nestled on a quiet island. Step inside to admire the monastery’s incredible colorful wall paintings, which bring to life ancient biblical stories in stunning detail.

After lunch prepare for an exciting excursion to the legendary Blue Nile Falls, locally called Tis Issat (“Smoking Water”). Enjoy a scenic walk through lush farmland and tranquil forests before reaching the roaring falls. Depending on the season, you’ll witness either a powerful, thundering cascade (rainy season) or elegant, misty streams (dry season) both equally breathtaking. As the day winds down, return to Bahir Dar.

itinerary.title: Bahir Dar – Gondar
paragraphs: Today, enjoy a beautiful drive through rolling green hills and traditional Ethiopian villages as we journey to Gondar. This historic city was once the imperial capital of Ethiopia, and visiting feels like traveling back in time!

After check in your reserved hotel our first stop is the famous Royal Enclosure, a UNESCO-listed site often called Africa’s Camelot. Walk among majestic 17th-century castles, including Fasiladas’ Palace with its grand towers and medieval-style arched windows.

Then, we visit the Debre Birhan Selassie Church (Light of Trinity), one of Ethiopia’s most treasured churches. Inside, you’ll be amazed by the brightly colored wall and ceiling paintings showing scenes from the Bible. Look up to see the famous ceiling of angel faces each one unique, representing God’s protection over the world.

itinerary.title: Gondar – Simien Mountains – Gondar
paragraphs: After breakfast, we’ll drive from Gondar to Debark, the gateway to the spectacular Simien Mountains National Park. Here, we’ll complete park entry formalities and meet our local scout for the adventure ahead. From Debark, we continue into the mountains, passing through the park entrance before arriving at Buit Ras, the starting point of our exploration. Prepare for a breathtaking scenic trek to Chilkuwanit, one of the park’s most magnificent viewpoints. Along the way, marvel the towering cliffs and dramatic escarpments, troops of playful Gelada Baboons (found only in Ethiopia) and possible sightings of jackals, klipspringers, and colorful birdlife.
After soaking in the panoramic views and wildlife encounters, we’ll return to Gondar.

itinerary.title: Gondar – Lalibela
paragraphs: On this day take a short flight to Lalibela, Ethiopia’s spiritual heart on the eve of Genna, the Ethiopian Christmas. As darkness falls, join devoted pilgrims at Bete Mariam Church for a mesmerizing candlelit ceremony. Clad in white robes, priests chant centuries-old hymns to the rhythmic pulse of kebero (drums). The scent of incense lingers in the air as worshippers fill the ancient rock-hewn courtyards, their faces illuminated by candlelight. At midnight, witness a sacred procession honoring Christ’s birth, where clergy carry replicas of the Ark of the Covenant in solemn reverence.

itinerary.title: Lalibela
paragraphs: On Christmas morning (called Genna in Ethiopia) wake up early, join the joyful celebration at Bete Mariam Church in Lalibela. The festivities begin before sunrise, as thousands of pilgrims dressed in white gather around the ancient rock-hewn church. Priests in colorful robes chant prayers, swing incense, and carry beautifully decorated tabots (replicas of the Ark of the Covenant) in a sacred procession. The air fills with the sound of drums, prayer sticks (mequamia), and the faithful singing hymns under the soft glow of candlelight.

After the sunrise service, the community shares a festive meal, breaking their 40-day fast with doro wat (spicy chicken stew), injera (sourdough flatbread), and honey wine (tej). Locals play Genna, a traditional hockey-like game, while children laugh and dance in celebration.

Spend the day exploring Bete Mariam’s and other rock hewn churches’ stunning architecture carved entirely from rock, with hidden tunnels and ancient religious art. As the sun sets, sip freshly brewed Ethiopian coffee with friendly locals, listening to stories of faith and history.
Genna in Lalibela is more than a holiday it’s a magical experience of devotion, culture, and warmth.

title: Timket Festival in Gondar
teaser: Ethiopian Epiphany at Fasilides’ Bath — processions of tabots, chanting priests and a joyous plunge into blessed water.
overview: Experience the Magic of Ethiopia: A Journey Through Culture, Faith & Natural Wonders. Immerse yourself in the vibrant energy of Ethiopia during Timkat, the country’s most spectacular religious festival. Witness priests in dazzling robes carrying sacred Tabots (replicas of the Ark of the Covenant) in a grand procession, accompanied by rhythmic drumming, hymns, and the joyful cheers of devotees. Feel the spiritual power as crowds gather for the holy water blessing, reenacting Jesus’ baptism in the Jordan River an unforgettable moment of devotion and celebration.

Beyond the festival, explore ancient castles, rock-hewn churches, and breathtaking landscapes. Step back in time at the Imperial Castle Compound, where emperors once ruled, and marvel at the stunning biblical murals inside historic churches. Venture into the Simien Mountains, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, where dramatic cliffs and rare gelada monkeys await. Discover the awe-inspiring rock-hewn churches of Lalibela, carved entirely from stone and hidden beneath the earth an architectural wonder unlike anywhere else in the world. Your adventure also includes scenic boat trips on Ethiopia’s largest lake, visits to colorful markets, and encounters with warm, welcoming communities. Savor delicious Ethiopian cuisine, rich with spices and tradition, and end your journey with a festive farewell dinner featuring cultural dances. This is more than a trip it’s a deep dive into history, faith, and natural beauty, leaving you with memories that will last a lifetime. Are you ready to explore the soul of Ethiopia?

After checking in at the hotel, embark on a private boat to visit Ura Kidane Mehret Ethiopian Orthodox Church, situated on the Zege Peninsula along Lake Tana. Founded in the 14th century, the current circular church structure dates back to the 16th century. Its interior is adorned with numerous murals painted between 100 and 250 years ago.
In the afternoon enjoy lunch, then drive to the village of Tis Isat to see the Blue Nile Falls. After the visit, return to Bahir Dar.

itinerary.title: Bahir Dar – Gondar
paragraphs: Celebrating Timkat in Gondar is a mesmerizing experience, especially during the Ketera procession on the eve of this grand Ethiopian Orthodox festival.

After breakfast, you’ll drive from Bahir Dar to Gondar, arriving in time to witness the vibrant religious ceremonies. Ketera marks the beginning of Timkat (Epiphany), where priests carry the sacred Tabot (a replica of the Ark of the Covenant) from the churches in a grand procession to Fasilides’ Bath. The streets come alive with the sounds of prayer, rhythmic drumming, and the sight of crowds dressed in dazzling white traditional garments, holding colorful umbrellas and crosses. The faithful follow the clergy in joyous celebration, singing hymns and chanting psalms as the Tabot is escorted to its temporary resting place near the water. After witnessing this awe-inspiring ceremony, you’ll return to your hotel to rest and prepare for the next day’s festivities, ensuring you’re refreshed for the spiritual and cultural experiences ahead. This is a rare opportunity to immerse yourself in Ethiopia’s deep religious traditions, surrounded by the historic beauty of Gondar.
Note: Since Timkat involves large crowds and long ceremonies, comfortable shoes, respectful clothing, and a reusable water bottle are recommended.

itinerary.title: Gondar
paragraphs: This day early in the morning, you will join the celebration of early Timkat mass program at Taboat Maderia to witness the beautiful baptism rituals at Fasilides Bath. The holy water symbolizes the Jordan River, as in the Bible. A priest blesses the water, and then a high-ranking clergy member dips a golden cross into it. He uses the water to put out a candle’s flame on the altar before sprinkling it over the crowd, a symbolic reenactment of Jesus’ baptism. After the ceremony, the sacred Tabots (replicas of the Ark of the Covenant) are carried back to their churches in a lively procession. The streets fill with joyful celebrations singing, dancing, and feasting as people follow the Tabots. Feel free to join the dancing with your guide and experience this unforgettable cultural tradition!

itinerary.title: Gondar
paragraphs: After breakfast, we begin our visit to the Imperial Castle Compound, the grand palace of Emperor Fasilidas and his successors. Explore the ancient halls, towers, and royal buildings while learning about Ethiopia’s fascinating history.
Next, we visit Quskuam Mariam Church, a beautiful 18th-century church built by Empress Mintwab. This sacred site holds deep religious significance and features traditional Gondarine architecture.

Finally, we enter the world-famous Debre Birhan Selassie Church, known as the “Light of Trinity.” Marvel at its stunning wall and ceiling paintings, which depict biblical stories in vibrant colors. The most famous highlight is the ceiling covered with angel faces, symbolizing God’s watchful protection.

itinerary.title: Gondar – Simien Mountains – Gondar
paragraphs: Set off early from Gondar for an unforgettable day exploring the Simien Mountains National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site known for its jaw-dropping scenery and unique wildlife. After a 2.5-hour scenic drive through rolling hills and rural villages, you’ll arrive at the park headquarters in Debark to pick up permits and meet your local guide. Then, a short drive to Sankaber takes you along dramatic cliffs and lush valleys, where you’ll almost certainly spot troops of playful gelada monkeys often called “bleeding-heart baboons” for their distinctive red chest patches. Keep an eye out for soaring birds of prey and other wildlife animals found only in these highlands. Enjoy a picnic lunch with panoramic views before heading back to Gondar in the late afternoon, stopping at viewpoints for last-minute photos of the breathtaking landscapes. This compact adventure packs in the best of the Simiens epic vistas, fascinating wildlife, and fresh mountain air all in one day!

In the afternoon, visit the remaining churches: Bete Amanuel, Bete Markorios, Bete Aba Libanos, and Bete Gebriel-Rufael.

itinerary.title: Lalibela
paragraphs: After a delicious breakfast, get ready for another incredible day exploring the legendary rock-hewn churches of Lalibela! Today, you’ll visit the remaining awe-inspiring churches you didn’t see on the first day, each one a masterpiece of ancient engineering and devotion. But the adventure doesn’t stop there. You’ll also take a scenic excursion outside Lalibela town to discover hidden gems like the stunning Genete Mariam rock-hewn church and others, carved into the rugged landscapes centuries ago. These lesser-known treasures offer a quieter, equally breathtaking experience, giving you a deeper connection to Ethiopia’s rich spiritual heritage.

itinerary.title: Lalibela – Addis Ababa (flight)
paragraphs: In the morning, take a domestic flight from Lalibela to Addis Ababa. Use your last few hours in Ethiopia for some final souvenir shopping to pick up beautiful handicrafts, aromatic coffee, and other local treasures at one of the city’s bustling markets.

Later, enjoy a farewell dinner at a traditional Ethiopian restaurant, where you’ll savor delicious local dishes while watching captivating cultural dances. Afterward, transfer to the airport for your departure.

title: Photography Tour: Omo Valley & Lalibela
teaser: A small-group photography journey timed for the best light among the Hamar, Karo, Dassanech and Mursi, ending in Lalibela.
overview: Ethiopia’s is rich diverse ethnographic attractions attributed to its nations, nationalities, and peoples of more than 83 languages and 200 dialects. One of the most important locations for these ethnographic tourism attractions is the lower Omo Valley of Southern Ethiopia which is home to an astonishing mix of small, contrasting ethnic groups such as Gnangatom, Karo, Dassench, Bodi, Mursi, Surma, Arbore, and Hamer – some of the most fascinating people and cultures.

A trip through Ethiopia that focuses on the South of the country, inhabited by some of the most attractions of the country: the Dorze with their spectacular huts, the Konso, the Mursi warriors whose women wear the lip plate, the Karos with their body paints and the Hamers with their peculiar clothing and beautiful women who cover their bodies and hair with grease and reddish mud. An ethnic journey, designed to be able to contact the great human wealth that this part of Ethiopia.

itinerary.title: Addis Ababa
paragraphs: The group members will be arriving at different times throughout the day from various international destinations. Since their flights are not synchronized, we will coordinate their arrivals accordingly. If, however, everyone arrives in Addis Ababa (Bole International Airport) around the same time or from the same origin, we can organize a short city tour or sightseeing activity while waiting for the rest of the group. For those arriving much earlier or later, we will arrange airport transfers and accommodations as planned. Please share your flight details in advance so we can optimize the schedule.

itinerary.title: Addis Ababa
paragraphs: Begin your Addis Ababa sightseeing with a scenic drive north to Mount Entoto, offering breathtaking views from its 3200m peak. Descending, you’ll visit the Ethnographic Museum, showcasing a comprehensive array of Ethiopian crafts and historically significant items. The National Museum awaits with its remarkable archaeological finds, including the iconic 3.4-million-year-old ‘Lucy’ fossil. After lunch, explore the grandeur of Trinity Cathedral, the largest and most revered church in Addis Ababa, built in 1941 and notable for its art and architecture. Your tour culminates with a drive through Merkato, Africa’s largest open-air market, a bustling hub of trade and local life.

itinerary.title: Addis Ababa – Arba Minch (flight)
paragraphs: Begin your day with an early breakfast before transferring to the airport to catch your morning flight to Arba Minch. Upon arrival, our drivers will take you to your accommodation. In the afternoon, visit the Dorze Village, renowned for its unique cultural traditions. The Dorze people are celebrated for their exceptional weaving craftsmanship, a skill passed down through generations. Other distinctive practices include producing local liquors, playing traditional music, and crafting food from the false banana plant (kocho). The Dorze community, who reside on lush hillsides, are also famous for their towering beehive-shaped huts—a remarkable architectural feat that reflects their ingenuity.

itinerary.title: Arba Minch – Turmi
paragraphs: This morning, after having early breakfast we take a boat cruise across the waters of Lake Chamo. Our destination is the renowned “Azo Gebeya,” or ‘crocodile market,’ a truly spectacular sight where an impressive number of large crocodiles gather. Keep your cameras ready for glimpses of wallowing hippos and the diverse and colorful birdlife that thrives in this ecosystem. Later, our overland journey southwards leads us towards Turmi. Our exploration includes a visit to a traditional Konso village, nestled within a striking landscape of gently sloping, terraced hills, recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage site. The Konso people are widely respected for their diligent nature, evident in the meticulously crafted terraces that carpet their hillsides, surprisingly producing some of the country’s most exceptional coffee. Their ancient artistic heritage is manifested in the distinctive totems that mark the final resting places of their ancestors. As we travel, we look forward to fascinating cultural exchanges, encountering the unique customs and traditions of the various tribes that inhabit this captivating region.

itinerary.title: Turmi – Omorate – Turmi
paragraphs: On this day after breakfast, our day unfolds with an excursion to Omorate, where we’ll have the privilege of meeting the Dassanech people – often called the ‘people of the Delta’ – who make their home along the northern shores of the vast Lake Turkana. After our visit, we’ll journey back to Turmi. The afternoon brings an encounter with the captivating Hamar people in their village. Renowned as one of the most striking and proud communities in the Omo Valley, the Hamar truly embody a sense of beauty and grace. Their women are particularly eye-catching, adorned in elegant leather skirts embellished with delicate, tiny pearls. Intricate and elaborate hairstyles serve as another significant form of their personal expression and beauty.

itinerary.title: Turmi – Nyangatom/Karo – Turmi
paragraphs: Begin your day with an early departure from Turmi, heading toward the remote village of Kangatan. From there, take a guided walk through lush fields, where locals tend to their crops, before arriving at a traditional Nyangatom tribal village. Immerse yourself in their vibrant culture, learning about their unique customs, intricate beadwork, and pastoral way of life.

After the visit, journey back across the river and continue to the spectacular Karo village of Korcho, perched dramatically on a Cliffside with breathtaking views over the Omo River. The Karo people, though the smallest tribe in the Omo Valley, are renowned for their stunning body paintings and elaborate scarification, making them some of the most visually striking communities in the region. Spend time interacting with the villagers, capturing their artistry, and admiring their striking traditional adornments.
Afterwards, we will enjoy a scenic drive back to Turmi, reflecting on the unforgettable cultural encounters of the day.

itinerary.title: Turmi – Jinka
paragraphs: After breakfast, drive to Jinka, stopping at Dimeka, home to one of Ethiopia’s most vibrant weekly markets (Tuesdays & Saturdays). Here, you’ll see the Hamer, Benna, Tsemai, Ari, and Karo tribes trading goods, dressed in traditional attire. Soak in the lively atmosphere before continuing through scenic landscapes to Jinka, the cultural heart of the Omo Valley.

itinerary.title: Jinka – Bodi/Mursi – Jinka
paragraphs: We’ll wake up early drive towards Mago National Park, a wild and beautiful area home to some of Ethiopia’s most iconic tribes. Our focus today is meeting the Bodi (known for their honey-colored body paint and unique ceremonies) and the Mursi (famous for their striking lip plates and decorative scarifications). These tribes have preserved their ancient customs in remarkable ways, and visiting their villages gives us a rare glimpse into traditions that have remained unchanged for generations. The drive itself is an adventure, with scenic landscapes and possible wildlife sightings along the way! After a visit drive back to Jinka.

itinerary.title: Mizan – Kibish

itinerary.title: Kibish
paragraphs: Spend the entire day immersed in the customs and daily life of the Surma people. Witness their elaborate body painting, intricate scarification, and perhaps even a ceremonial Donga (stick-fighting) event, a significant cultural practice among the Surma.

itinerary.title: Kibish – Nyangatom
paragraphs: Continue the journey to Nyangatom, another remarkable tribe in the Lower Omo Valley. The Nyangatom, known for their distinctive adornments and pastoral lifestyle, provide another fascinating cultural encounter.

itinerary.title: Nyangatom – Karo – Turmi
paragraphs: Travel to the Karo people, renowned for their intricate body painting and riverside villages. After spending time with the Karo, proceed to Turmi, the heart of Hamar territory, where vibrant traditions and lively ceremonies await.

itinerary.title: Turmi – Omorate – Turmi
paragraphs: Venture to Omorate to meet the Dassanech people, who inhabit the banks of the Omo River. Cross the river by boat to visit their remote villages before returning to Turmi for another evening among the Hamar.

itinerary.title: Turmi – Arbore – Turmi
paragraphs: Explore the Arbore tribe, known for their colorful beadwork and unique spiritual beliefs. Learn about their role as intermediaries between neighboring tribes before heading back to Turmi.

itinerary.title: Turmi – Jinka
paragraphs: Depart Turmi and drive to Jinka, the gateway to Mago National Park. En route, enjoy the shifting landscapes and prepare for the next day’s encounter with the Mursi people.

itinerary.title: Jinka – Bodi/Mursi – Jinka
paragraphs: Venture into Mago National Park to visit the Mursi, famous for their lip plates and striking adornments. Alternatively, meet the Bodi people, known for their unique Ka’el ceremony. Return to Jinka in the evening.

itinerary.title: Jinka – Addis Ababa (flight)
paragraphs: Take a morning flight back to Addis Ababa, where you can enjoy some last-minute shopping or sightseeing before your departure.
Extension to Lalibela Itinerary

itinerary.title: Addis Ababa – Lalibela (flight)
paragraphs: After breakfast, take a short flight to Lalibela. After checking in at the hotel, visit the rock-hewn Churches of Lalibela. Lalibela is the jewel in the crown of Ethiopia, home to the most famous churches and the scene of many major religious ceremonies. Also known as ‘Africa’s Petra’, Lalibela and its rock-hewn churches are among Ethiopia’s top attractions. Visit the churches: Bete Medhane Alem, Bete Mariam, Bete Maskal, Bete Danaghel, Bete Golgotha & Bete Mikael, and Bete Giorgis. In the afternoon, visit the remaining churches: Bete Amanuel, Bete Markorios, Bete Aba Libanos, and Bete Gebriel-Rufael.

itinerary.title: Lalibela
paragraphs: After breakfast, visit the rest of the rock-hewn churches of Lalibela and take an excursion to visit some of the churches outside Lalibela town.

itinerary.title: Lalibela – Addis Ababa (flight)
paragraphs: Take a morning flight back to Addis Ababa, where you can enjoy some last-minute shopping or sightseeing before your departure.
